data_sources.notes: The new diagnosis method should reuse this exact ownership check verbatim — refusing a trace that does not belong to this run is not a nicety, the ids are content hashes so a mismatch is a request for another experiment's evidence. Note what the existing endpoint does NOT return: v and omega are dropped from the payload, so the browser cannot compute oscillation client-side even though the column exists in the file.

rules.claim: this episode's trajectory can be analysed over time
rules.condition: outcome.row_count == 1 and outcome.terminal_event == 'no_path' — nav_stack.py lines 439-444 writes exactly one row at t=0.0 at the start pose when the global plan fails, so travel_time_s == 0 and every time-series signal is undefined
rules.suggested_action: read plan.global_plan_time_ms and plan.peak_search_nodes — the only evidence this file carries — and inspect the map and mission endpoints rather than the trajectory
rules.forbidden_action: never report clearance-over-time, oscillation, stop-and-go or replan statistics for a one-row trace, and never report their zero values as measurements; they are undefined, not zero

rules.claim: the episode ended in a collision at a locatable instant
rules.condition: outcome.terminal_event == 'collision'; the instant is the LAST row (SimulationEngine._check_termination terminates on first contact, so a trace carries at most one collision event and it is always the final row)
rules.suggested_action: read clearance.at_failure_m and contact.dynamic_obstacles_declared together — the pose is exact, the attribution is not
rules.forbidden_action: never say what the robot hit on the strength of the trace alone; the event vocabulary has one token 'collision' and clearance_m is a scalar minimum over grid, static shapes and moving circles with no attribution

rules.claim: the collision can be blamed on a specific obstacle
rules.condition: outcome.terminal_event == 'collision' and (contact.dynamic_obstacles_declared == 0 or contact.nearest_surface_distance_m > EPS) — either the profile declares no traffic, or every recomputed dynamic obstacle is clear of the robot at t_fail, which leaves the static map or a static shape as the only remaining explanation and the trace cannot say which
rules.suggested_action: re-derive the contact from the map and profile.environment.static geometry, or re-run the episode with the same context and read EpisodeResult.reason, which names 'static obstacle' or 'dynamic obstacle'
rules.forbidden_action: never name a cell, wall or shape as the thing struck; the file records no obstacle identity at all

rules.claim: the robot kept a working margin from obstacles
rules.condition: clearance.seconds_below_warning > 0, where the threshold is profile.constraints.clearance_warning_m and dwell[i] = t[i+1] - t[i] with dwell[last] = 0.0. Report clearance.n_warning_intervals (maximal runs of consecutive samples below the threshold) beside it, never the raw sample count
rules.suggested_action: compare clearance.longest_warning_interval_s with the episode's travel time and look at clearance.min_t_s to see whether the margin was lost once or repeatedly
rules.forbidden_action: never quote the number of below-threshold SAMPLES as a number of near misses; a real stuck trace holds 201 consecutive such samples over 10.05 s, which is one approach, not 201 — and never restate this as HĐ-6's near_miss_rate, which is a different quantity normalised by path length

rules.claim: clearance_m measures how much room the robot had
rules.condition: clearance.censored_sample_fraction > 0, computed as the fraction of samples with clearance_m >= (DEFAULT_CLEARANCE_WINDOW_M - profile.robot.radius) - EPS. clearance_to_grid_within saturates at window - radius, so values at the ceiling mean 'at least this much', not 'exactly this much'
rules.suggested_action: read clearance.min_m and the below-warning statistics, which sit far under the ceiling and are exact; ignore the upper tail
rules.forbidden_action: never report a mean clearance, a clearance trend, or 'the robot had N metres of room' from censored samples; in a real trace 150 of 420 samples (36%) sit exactly at 1.74 m, and warehouse_a_v2's own recorded closest approach to its forklift, 2.53 m, is above the ceiling and therefore absent from the column entirely

rules.claim: the robot was making progress when the episode ended
rules.condition: motion.seconds_rotating_in_place >= 0.25 * outcome.travel_time_s, where a sample counts when abs(v) <= STOP_SPEED_EPS (1e-3, reused from definitions.py) and abs(omega) > motion.omega_deadband_rad_s, weighted by dwell
rules.suggested_action: read it beside motion.sign_changes and progress.stalled_seconds — spinning with no sign changes is a controller committed to one turn direction, not an oscillation
rules.forbidden_action: never call this oscillation, and never call it a controller command; v and omega are the achieved RobotState, so the evidence supports 'the robot rotated without translating', not 'the controller commanded a spin'

rules.claim: the controller drove a settled course
rules.condition: motion.sign_changes_in_window >= OSCILLATION_MIN_SIGN_FLIPS (6) and motion.window_displacement_m <= OSCILLATION_MAX_DISPLACEMENT (0.5), over the last OSCILLATION_WINDOW_SECONDS (4.0) — the same three constants failure.py already uses. Counting: s_i = sign(omega_i) if abs(omega_i) > deadband else 0; drop the zeros; count adjacent pairs whose product is negative
rules.suggested_action: cross-read motion.sign_changes_per_s over the whole episode; a burst in the final window is a different fault from steady chatter throughout
rules.forbidden_action: never report a sign-change count without its deadband and window; a bare count over an undeaded omega column counts numerical zero-crossings of a robot driving straight. And never conclude 'no oscillation' from a low count alone — a real stuck trace scores 1 sign change while spending 9.55 s of 20.95 s rotating in place

rules.claim: the episode ended for a reason visible at the final instant
rules.condition: outcome.terminal_event == 'stuck'; the engine fired because displacement over the last scenario.stuck_time_window (= profile.constraints.stuck_threshold_s) fell below stuck_min_displacement, so the informative interval is [outcome.stuck_window_start_s, outcome.t_fail_s], defined for every episode as max(t[0], t_fail - stuck_threshold_s)
rules.suggested_action: read what happened inside that window — motion.seconds_rotating_in_place, clearance in the window, replan.indices — rather than the final row alone
rules.forbidden_action: never distinguish a wedged robot from one that kept moving without approaching the goal; trace.py's _STATUS_TO_EVENT maps BOTH EpisodeStatus.STUCK and EpisodeStatus.NO_PROGRESS to the single token 'stuck', and the file cannot separate them

rules.claim: the stuck verdict was reached against thresholds this deployment declared
rules.condition: outcome.terminal_event == 'stuck' — always, because scenario_for() bridges only stuck_time_window from the profile; Scenario.stuck_min_displacement (0.05 m), progress_time_window (30.0 s) and progress_min_decrease (0.05 m) are simulator defaults no TaskProfile field sets
rules.suggested_action: decide whether 0.05 m in the deployment's stuck window is the standstill this warehouse means, and add the field to TaskConstraints if it is not
rules.forbidden_action: never present stuck_min_displacement, progress_time_window or progress_min_decrease as thresholds the deployment chose; nobody declared them

rules.claim: the episode ran out of time while still working toward the goal
rules.condition: outcome.terminal_event == 'timeout' and progress.stalled_seconds >= profile.constraints.stuck_threshold_s, where goal_distance_m[i] = hypot(x_i - goal.x, y_i - goal.y) against the mission goal from the EpisodeContext, and t_last_progress_s is the last t at which goal_distance fell below its running minimum by more than EPS
rules.suggested_action: read progress.min_goal_distance_m and its timestamp — a robot that got close and then drifted back is a different fault from one that never approached
rules.forbidden_action: never describe straight-line goal distance as path progress; a legitimate detour increases it, which is the same caveat failure.py already attaches to FAILURE_TO_PROGRESS

rules.claim: the stack could not reach the goal
rules.condition: outcome.terminal_event == 'timeout' and progress.goal_distance_at_end_m <= 5 * profile.constraints.goal_tolerance_m — the same 'close' rule failure.py uses at line 164
rules.suggested_action: treat this as too slow rather than lost, and check travel_time against episode_timeout_s before blaming the planner
rules.forbidden_action: never claim the goal was effectively reached; HĐ-6's _goal_reached requires both the recorded goal_reached event AND the profile's tolerance, and this episode has neither

rules.claim: the stack recovered by replanning
rules.condition: replan.count >= 3, counted as rows with event == 'replan' — the same definition HĐ-6's replan_count uses (definitions.py line 221). Report replan.inter_replan_s so a burst is distinguishable from a steady trickle
rules.suggested_action: read replan.excess_ms_total beside travel_time_s: replanning is charged in time and latency, not in a separate penalty
rules.forbidden_action: never score replanning; it is evidence, never an objective term (definitions.py's replan_count docstring is explicit that a penalty would price the same thing twice)

rules.claim: the replan counts describe replans that produced a path
rules.condition: replan.count > 0 — always. nav_stack.py line 573 increments pending_replan_ms for EVERY attempt, and the next control step is marked event='replan' whether new_plan.success was True or False; the distinction lives only in EpisodeResult.events as type='replan_failed', which is never written to Parquet
rules.suggested_action: re-run the episode with the same context and read EpisodeResult.events if the successful/failed split matters, or extend TRACE_EVENTS with a 'replan_failed' token and bump the contract
rules.forbidden_action: never say how many replans found a route; 'replanned eleven times, eight of which found nothing' — the single most useful sentence about a failed recovery — is not computable from this file

rules.claim: the replan cost N milliseconds
rules.condition: replan.count > 0. On a replan row planner_latency_ms = decision.latency_seconds*1000 + pending_replan_ms (nav_stack.py line 509), a sum whose halves the file does not separate. The only honest figure is an excess: excess_ms[i] = max(0, planner_latency_ms[i] - replan.baseline_step_latency_ms), where the baseline is the median over non-replan, non-terminal rows
rules.suggested_action: sanity-check the estimate against metadata.global_plan_time_ms for the initial plan — 572.6 ms against a ~5 ms per-step baseline in a real trace, so a replan row stands out by two orders of magnitude
rules.forbidden_action: never present the excess as a measured global-planning time; it is a subtraction against a median, and it is labelled an estimate or it is not reported

rules.claim: every replan the episode paid for is marked as one
rules.condition: replan.unmarked_terminal_cost_ms > 0, i.e. the last row carries planner_latency_ms > 0 while its event is a terminal status rather than 'replan'. nav_stack.py line 646 charges any pending_replan_ms to the verdict row, so the final replan of a recovery the episode outlived is priced but unlabelled
rules.suggested_action: add this to the replan cost estimate and note that the event count is one lower than the attempts the episode paid for
rules.forbidden_action: never treat the terminal row's planner_latency_ms as a control-step latency; it is not one, yet HĐ-6's p99_latency_ms pools it with the rest

rules.claim: the stack was meeting its control deadline when the episode failed
rules.condition: latency.ms_at_failure > profile.robot.t_cycle_ms, or latency.max_ms > t_cycle_ms with latency.max_t_s inside the failure window
rules.suggested_action: compare with the candidate's pooled G4 figure in report['candidates'][i]['gates']['G4']['p99_ms'] — one late step is not a gate verdict
rules.forbidden_action: never recompute a p99 over a different row population and present it beside G4's; G4's number is pooled over every control step of the whole evaluation set (pooled_p99_latency_ms), and a per-episode percentile is a different statistic

rules.claim: clearance.min_m is the closest the robot ever came
rules.condition: sampling.rows_per_sim_step < 1.0, i.e. the median row spacing exceeds scenario.simulation_dt = min(MAX_SIMULATION_DT (0.05), profile.robot.control_period). Rows are control ticks (nav_stack.py line 504-506) while _check_termination runs every simulation step, so unrecorded sim steps sit between rows
rules.suggested_action: read clearance.min_m as an upper bound on the true minimum; the exact minimum would need a trace written per simulation step
rules.forbidden_action: never state a minimum clearance as exact when rows are coarser than the engine. Not currently triggered by the shipped profiles — open_hall_v2 and warehouse_a_v2 both declare control_period 0.05 so rows and sim steps coincide — but validate_control_rate permits a controller period up to the deployment's, and the registry's LocalControllerConfig.control_period defaults to 0.1

rules.claim: this trace records how the episode ended
rules.condition: outcome.terminal_event_present is False, i.e. event[-1] is null. event_for_status returns None for EpisodeStatus.RUNNING and EpisodeStatus.STOPPED, and a crashed episode leaves whatever the context manager flushed
rules.suggested_action: check whether the episode was stopped by an operator or the process died; do not count it as a candidate failure either way
rules.forbidden_action: never infer a failure reason for a trace with no terminal event, and never let HĐ-6's fallback — _failure_reason returns 'stuck' when no terminal event is present — be read as a measured diagnosis; it is an explicit last resort because HĐ-6 fixes four buckets

rules.claim: the trace shows why the controller stopped commanding motion
rules.condition: always, for any episode ending 'stuck' or 'timeout'. The local planner reports decision.failure_reason ('found no safe velocity and commanded a stop'), nav_stack.py lines 524-531 collects it into EpisodeResult.events as type='local_planner_failure', and TRACE_EVENTS has no token for it
rules.suggested_action: read v, omega and clearance in the stuck window as the nearest available proxy, and consider extending TRACE_EVENTS with a 'local_planner_failure' token
rules.forbidden_action: never assert the local planner found no safe velocity; the most explanatory signal for a stuck episode is measured by the simulator and then discarded before the file is written

risks: HĐ-15.3 double-definition risk. definitions.py is 'the one place a metric is defined'. min_clearance, replan_count, travel_time_s, failure_reason, p99_latency_ms and smoothness ALL already exist there. If the diagnosis recomputes any of them, two modules can disagree and a Decision Card and a failure explanation will quote different numbers for the same episode. Mitigation: diagnose_episode(trace, profile, context, *, metrics: EpisodeMetricSet | None = None) copies those values, never derives them, and publishes no field bearing an HĐ-6 name that it computed itself. The argmin INDEX of clearance is new and is the only thing the diagnosis derives from that column.

resolve() cannot distinguish a missing path from a null value (self_check.py lines 103-110 return None for both), and critique() line 515 drops findings on that test. A rule that cites a legitimately-null field is silently deleted — the failure mode is invisible because the finding simply does not appear. Every rule above therefore cites an int/float/bool. This must be enforced by a test that asserts resolve(diagnosis_dict, rule.field_path) is not None for every rule over a fixture set covering all five terminal events.

The EpisodeContext is not in the trace. TraceMetadata carries episode_context_id (a hash) and task_profile_id but neither mission_id nor seed, so goal distance and dynamic-obstacle attribution are unavailable without an external context record. For runs with a decision card it comes from report['manifest']['episode_contexts']['evaluation']; for gate-only runs report['manifest'] is None (selection.py line 723) and the only path is regenerating with build_evaluation_contexts and matching by id. Gate-only runs are exactly the runs most likely to be full of failures, so the degraded path is the common path. Regeneration must match by episode_context_id and refuse on no match, never assume positional order.

Recomputing dynamic-obstacle positions contradicts a docstring the codebase relies on. trace.py lines 18-23 justify recording clearance_m by asserting positions cannot be re-derived; dynamic.py's position_at says they are a pure function of (spec, time, seed) with no hidden state. Both are true of different things — the Metrics Engine may read only the file, while the explainer legitimately holds the profile and the context — but shipping code that acts on the second reading while the first is still written down invites somebody to 'fix' one of them. Either the trace docstring gets a sentence, or the attribution feature does not ship.

Threshold invention. HĐ-7 forbids a bar nobody set, and the oscillation deadband and the 0.25-of-travel-time rotation trigger are bars nobody set. definitions.py has an accepted precedent for this (STOP_SPEED_EPS = 1e-3, documented as 'a reporting convention rather than a deployment threshold — no candidate is judged on it'), and the diagnosis must inherit that framing explicitly: nothing here feeds a gate, an objective or a ranking, and every constant is published in the payload under `thresholds` so a reader can see what was applied.

Rate-vs-count confusion in clearance. The obvious implementation counts samples below the warning threshold, which is meaningless without the sample rate: a real trace holds 201 consecutive such samples spanning 10.05 s, and the same approach at a 0.1 s control period would count 100. Everything time-like must be dwell-weighted with dwell[i] = t[i+1] - t[i] and dwell[last] = 0.0, and the interval count must be maximal runs, not samples.

The censoring ceiling is not theoretical. 36% of samples in the one real trace examined sit exactly at 2.0 - robot_radius, and warehouse_a_v2's own recorded closest forklift approach (2.53 m) is above the ceiling and therefore invisible. Any prose the LLM writes about 'how much room' will be wrong for the majority of samples unless the payload hands it the censored fraction and the rule bans the claim.

Non-uniform row spacing. The 12 real traces on disk all have dt exactly 0.05, which will make a naive implementation look correct and hide every unit bug. A controller running at 0.1 s (the registry default) with an engine at 0.05 s produces half-rate rows, and the terminal verdict row lands at an arbitrary t off any grid. Fixtures must include a non-uniform trace.

No failed episode of the interesting kinds exists on disk. All 12 traces under artifacts/traces/ end in goal_reached (9) or stuck (3). There is no collision trace, no timeout trace, no no_path trace and no replan trace anywhere in the repository, so every branch that matters is unexercised by real data and must be covered by synthetically written traces (tests/test_metric_definitions.py lines 102-148 already has a write_trace/straight_run helper pair to copy).

The LLM layer inherits critique.py's banned-language rule (assert_no_banned_language, BANNED_PHRASES = ('an toàn', 'TCO')) and it bites harder here: prose about a collision is exactly where a model reaches for 'unsafe'. The Vietnamese pattern is a plain substring match on 'an\s+toàn' in either polarity, so the ban applies to 'không an toàn' too. The prose must be dropped and the deterministic findings kept, as critique.py lines 375-380 do.
open_questions: Does the diagnosis take a pre-computed EpisodeMetricSet, or call compute_metrics itself? Calling it requires map_data (for reference_path_length) and can raise MetricError — including the goal_reached-outside-tolerance refusal, which would make the explainer crash on precisely the malformed episode somebody wants explained. Recommendation: accept `metrics: EpisodeMetricSet | None = None`, degrade gracefully when it is None, and let the API pass the one it already has. Needs your call because it decides whether the module can be used standalone on a bare Parquet file.

Should _failure_reason be promoted from private to public in definitions.py? The diagnosis needs HĐ-6's four-bucket precedence (collision > no_path > timeout > stuck). Copying it creates the second definition HĐ-15.3 forbids; promoting it is a one-line public rename in the module the decision layer reads. Recommend promoting.

What is the oscillation deadband? failure.py uses an absolute 0.1 rad/s. Expressing it as a fraction of profile.robot.max_angular_velocity (0.1/1.2 ≈ 8% for the shipped profiles) is more in the spirit of HĐ-7 but changes the number relative to the existing detector, and two modules disagreeing about what counts as an oscillation is its own problem. Recommend reusing the absolute 0.1 and importing the constant from failure.py rather than re-declaring it — which raises the next question.

May packages/metrics import from packages/benchmark? The four oscillation constants (OSCILLATION_MIN_SIGN_FLIPS, OSCILLATION_WINDOW_SECONDS, OSCILLATION_MAX_DISPLACEMENT, LOW_CLEARANCE_FRACTION_OF_RADIUS) live in planbench_benchmark.failure, and today metrics does not import benchmark — benchmark imports metrics (pipeline.py). Importing upward would invert that edge. The alternatives are moving the constants down into schemas or metrics, or duplicating them. Needs a decision before the first line is written.

Does the old planbench_benchmark.failure module stay? It is dead outside tests, it answers the same question from a data source (EpisodeResult) the decision layer no longer produces (nav_stack is called with legacy_metrics=False in the contract path), and its FailureCategory vocabulary is richer than what a trace can support. Leaving both leaves two answers to 'why did this episode fail'. Options: retire it, or keep it explicitly labelled as the live-simulation path.

Should TRACE_EVENTS be extended? Two of the most explanatory signals are measured and then thrown away: 'replan_failed' (the expensive half of a failed recovery) and 'local_planner_failure' (found no safe velocity, commanded a stop). Both exist as EpisodeEvent objects in EpisodeResult and neither is writable to the Parquet because the vocabulary is closed at six tokens. Adding them is a contract change (HĐ-5 §0 says the schema is frozen) and would not apply retroactively to any trace already on disk. Worth costing: without them the explainer's answer for a stuck episode is 'the robot rotated in place for 9.55 s' rather than 'the controller found no safe velocity 47 times'.

Should STUCK and NO_PROGRESS get separate trace tokens? _STATUS_TO_EVENT collapses them, and they are opposite diagnoses — 'it stopped moving' points at the controller, 'it kept moving without getting closer' points at the route. Same contract-change cost as the previous question.

Should the existing trace endpoint start returning v and omega? It currently drops both from the payload (decision_service.py lines 566-579) even though they are in the file, so no client can plot or verify the oscillation numbers the diagnosis reports. Adding them is two lines and makes the deterministic half checkable by eye.

Where does dynamic-obstacle attribution live — in the diagnosis, or nowhere? It is exactly computable and it is the difference between 'clearance reached 0.00 m at t=41.3' and 'the forklift was 0.00 m away at t=41.3'. But it is a recomputation from the profile and the seed, not a reading of the file, and it needs the trace.py docstring corrected first. It is the single highest-value signal in this spec and the one most likely to be argued about.

Severity semantics. self_check's blocking/material/disclosure mean 'the conclusion does not stand / stands with a condition / stands but must be said out loud' — a statement about a decision run, not about a robot. This spec reads them as 'this is the recorded cause / a contributing factor that changes what you would fix / a property of the measurement the reader must know'. That reuse keeps one vocabulary across both critics and keeps the LLM's output schema identical, but the words are being stretched. Confirm before the enum is shared.

unbuildable_rules: THE STRUCTURAL BREAK — the draft's candidate entry cannot be one shape. PF_STACK_NOT_BENCHMARKABLE, PF_CONFIG_NOT_FOR_THIS_CONTROLLER, PF_MODEL_NOT_CHOSEN, PF_RL_RUNTIME_MISSING and PF_CONTROL_RATE_SLOWER_THAN_DEPLOYMENT all fire in exactly the situations where `candidate_from_stack` RAISES — so no `Candidate` exists and `candidate_id`/`observation_requirements`/`params` are unavailable. PF_DUPLICATE_CANDIDATE_ID, PF_OBSERVATION_NOT_AVAILABLE and PF_OBSERVATION_ASYMMETRY need precisely those built fields. The spec never pins the candidate entry shape, and `keep_resolvable` deletes without a trace, so roughly half the rule set would vanish at runtime with no error.

PF_MODEL_NOT_CHOSEN is unreachable, and not for the reason the spec's risks give. `build_candidates` (selection.py:172) always calls `candidate_from_stack(stack, params=dict(LOCAL_CONTROLLER_CONFIGS[local]))`, and `CONTROLLER_CONFIGS` (candidates.py:242) has only a `"dwa"` group. For `astar+ppo` any config therefore trips `_reject_unknown_params` (candidates.py:95) on velocity_samples/omega_samples/horizon_seconds BEFORE `validate_algorithm_config` ever reaches `PPOStackConfig._require_a_model` (registry.py:88). There is no params block to inspect and no Candidate to inspect it on.

PF_SCOPE_CANNOT_HOLD_LAYER_FIXED and PF_DUPLICATE_CANDIDATE_ID cannot both come from one `validate_experiment_scope` call. That function (candidate.py:389) raises on the FIRST problem: the duplicate-id loop (409-417) runs before the `full_stack_selection` early return (419) and before the fingerprint comparison (433). One call yields at most one exception. It also requires a list of built `Candidate` objects, so it cannot run at all when any candidate failed to build.

PF_CONTROL_RATE_SLOWER_THAN_DEPLOYMENT's instruction is self-contradictory. `validate_control_rate` (candidates.py:313) loops over every candidate and calls `build_local_planner(...)`, which for `astar+ppo` is `_build_ppo` — it checks `find_spec('stable_baselines3')` and loads a checkpoint. The function takes no skip parameter and has no per-candidate entry point, so 'call the validator, do not re-implement it' and 'guard the build for requires_model stacks' cannot both hold. It also raises on the first violation, so it can report at most one candidate.

PF_MAP_UNREADABLE lets the pre-flight raise. The spec catches only `MapLoadError`. `load_environment_map` (task_map.py:112) also propagates `MapServerFormatError` from `load_map_server` on a corrupt PGM/YAML, raises `MapProfileMismatch` from `_check_yaml_image_matches` (task_map.py:155) for an image/YAML pairing bug, and lets a bare `yaml.YAMLError`/`OSError` escape. An advisory endpoint that raises is worse than no advisory.

PF_MISSION_MAP_MISMATCH's 'one advice per problem sentence' forces the string-parsing the spec forbids elsewhere. `validate_missions_on_map` (task_map.py:194) accumulates a `problems: list[str]` and raises ONE `MapProfileMismatch` whose message is `'\n  '.join(problems)`. Recovering per-mission advices with per-mission field_paths means parsing that joined message. Worse, `_check_yaml_image_matches` raises the same exception type with a message containing no mission at all, so it would be rendered as a mission-shaped finding.

Hardcoded indices in field_paths. PF_DUPLICATE_CANDIDATE_ID cites `candidates[1].candidate_id`, PF_GOAL_CLEARANCE_TIGHT cites `task_profile.missions[0].goal`, PF_POSE_INSIDE_TRAFFIC and PF_TRAFFIC_NEVER_MEETS_MISSION cite `task_profile.environment.dynamic_obstacles[0].motion`. When the offender is not at that index the advice still RESOLVES and names the wrong object — which is the unverifiable-citation failure `keep_resolvable` exists to prevent, and it will not be caught.

PF_TRAFFIC_NEVER_MEETS_MISSION cannot detect the failure its own `do_not` cites. The warehouse_a incident was temporal, not geometric: the forklift's periodic segment is x=12, y in [4,18] (warehouse_a_v2.yaml), and the straight line from (2,3) to (38,21) passes through (12, 8.0) — dead centre of it. A reachable-set-versus-straight-line test fires on nothing there. Catching that case requires sampling `position_at(obstacle, t, seed)` (dynamic.py:124, pure) across the seed set.

PF_ZERO_VARIANCE_SEEDS reads `deterministic=False` off 'the candidate's config'. `deterministic` is a `PPOStackConfig` field (registry.py:81) and `Candidate.params` is keyed by controller NAME (`{'dwa': {...}}`, candidates.py:180) — so there is no fixed path to it, and today no PPO candidate can be registered at all.

PF_REPLANNING_TRIGGER_UNREACHABLE and PF_STUCK_NEVER_FIRES cite the same field_path (`task_profile.constraints.stuck_threshold_s`) and their conditions nest — both require `stuck_threshold_s >= episode_timeout_s`. On a replanning-enabled profile with a short timeout, two advices land on one field saying overlapping things.

CALIBRATION CLAIM IS FALSE. PF_NO_PATH_RATE_GRANULARITY fires on the shipped `open_hall_v2`: N_min = ceil(3/0.1) = 30, one mission so `episodes_per_candidate` = 30, and 0 < no_path_rate_max (0.02) < 1/30 (0.0333). The spec's central design argument — 'fires NOTHING on open_hall_v2, because a critic that flags the system for being honest stops being read' — does not hold as written. (warehouse_a_v2 is clean: 1/300 = 0.00333 < 0.02.)

PF_SCOPE_UNKNOWN and PF_SCOPE_CANNOT_HOLD_LAYER_FIXED double-fire on a typo. Confirmed at candidate.py:422-424: `fixed_layer = 'local' if scope == 'global_planner_selection' else 'global'`, so a typo'd scope is treated as layer-scoped on `global`. Two candidates with different global planners then trip the fingerprint check too, and the second advice is an artifact of the first.

PF_POSE_INSIDE_TRAFFIC / PF_TRAFFIC_NEVER_MEETS_MISSION under-state the random_walk reachable set. `_random_walk_position` (dynamic.py:193-216) tests the bound AFTER stepping and reflects toward the origin; from the origin itself `atan2(0,0)` is 0, so the first step goes +x unchecked. A position can exceed `max_radius` by up to `speed * change_interval`.
corrections: Freeze the candidate entry shape in `build_draft()` as a merged record, not a `Candidate.model_dump()`. Something like: `{'stack', 'local_config', 'buildable': bool, 'build_error': str|None, 'requires_model': bool|None, 'benchmarkable': bool|None, 'local_controller': str|None, 'global_observation_class': str|None, 'local_observation_class': str|None, 'candidate_id': str|None, 'observation_requirements': list|None, 'params': dict|None}` — request half always present, registry half filled from `algorithm_info(stack)` (which returns None rather than raising, registry.py:332), Candidate half filled only when `candidate_from_stack` succeeded. Note that `None` in any of these makes `resolve()` return None and `keep_resolvable` delete the advice, so a rule may only cite a slot it has just proved non-null.

Move `scope` into the `plan` block (or repoint PF_SCOPE_UNKNOWN and PF_SCOPE_CANNOT_HOLD_LAYER_FIXED at a top-level `scope`), and add `episodes_requested` to `plan` alongside `seed_count`, `episodes_per_candidate`, `n_min_required`, `episode_runs_total`. Pick one and write it into the spec — the rules and the resource currently disagree.

Repoint the three broken field_paths: PF_STACK_NOT_BENCHMARKABLE -> `candidates[i].stack`; PF_CONFIG_NOT_FOR_THIS_CONTROLLER and PF_CONTROL_RATE_SLOWER_THAN_DEPLOYMENT -> `candidates[i].local_config`; PF_MODEL_NOT_CHOSEN and PF_RL_RUNTIME_MISSING -> `candidates[i].requires_model` — all three keys only exist if the merged shape above is adopted. Verify each citation against a real draft dict in a test, the way tests/test_advice.py already does.
Replace every literal index with the real one: `candidates[{i}]`, `task_profile.missions[{i}].goal`, `task_profile.environment.dynamic_obstacles[{j}].motion`, `candidates[{dup_index}].candidate_id`.

Compute PF_DUPLICATE_CANDIDATE_ID directly from the built candidates' `candidate_id`s rather than from `validate_experiment_scope`, and call `validate_experiment_scope` only for the layer-fixed check — skipping it entirely when the scope is not one of `ExperimentScope`'s three members (so PF_SCOPE_UNKNOWN suppresses PF_SCOPE_CANNOT_HOLD_LAYER_FIXED), and skipping it when any candidate failed to build.

Resolve the PF_CONTROL_RATE contradiction by reading the declared period out of the validated config instead of building. For a `requires_model` stack that is `PPOStackConfig.control_period` (default 0.1, registry.py:85); for DWA it is `LOCAL_CONTROLLER_CONFIGS[local]['control_period']`. Say in `ground` which of the two was used, as the spec's own risk note asks. Alternatively add a `build: Callable` or `skip_ids` parameter to `validate_control_rate` — but that is a change to a validator on the launch path and needs its own approval.

Widen PF_MAP_UNREADABLE to catch `MapLoadError`, `MapServerFormatError`, `MapProfileMismatch` raised from `_check_yaml_image_matches`, and a final `except Exception` that degrades to a single advice — `preflight()` must never raise. For PF_MISSION_MAP_MISMATCH, extract the problem list from `validate_missions_on_map` into a non-raising `mission_map_problems(profile, map_data) -> tuple[tuple[str, str], ...]` (mission id, sentence) in task_map.py, and have `validate_missions_on_map` raise off it. Fix the calibration story: either raise the PF_NO_PATH_RATE_GRANULARITY threshold so it does not fire at N=30 on a 0.02 no-path allowance, drop the rule, or amend the spec to state honestly that open_hall_v2 draws one disclosure advice and argue why that is acceptable. Do not leave the false 'fires NOTHING' claim in place — it is the evidence the whole advisory layer's credibility rests on.

Reword PF_TRAFFIC_NEVER_MEETS_MISSION's `do_not` so it stops claiming the warehouse_a lineage, OR change the rule to sample `position_at(obstacle, t, seed)` over the draft's seed range and check spatio-temporal proximity to a straight-line traverse. As written the rule is geometric and the incident was temporal.
Add `speed * change_interval` slack to the random_walk reachable disk (dynamic.py:193-216 can leave the disk), and state the padding in `ground`.
Deduplicate PF_STUCK_NEVER_FIRES against PF_REPLANNING_TRIGGER_UNREACHABLE — suppress the former when the latter fires, or give them distinct field_paths (`episode_timeout_s` vs `stuck_threshold_s`).

Route mechanics, confirmed and simpler than the spec suggests: `POST /decisions/preflight` collides with nothing (every existing POST under /decisions is either static — `/decisions/jobs` — or two segments with a static suffix), so no ordering care is needed. For the base_dir risk, `get_map_root` (dependencies.py:114) returns `state.decision_map_root`, which is the SAME object passed to `DecisionRunService` as `repo_root` (dependencies.py:167). Declare the existing `MapRoot = Annotated[Path, Depends(get_map_root)]` on the route — it is already imported in decisions.py:61 — and the pre-flight and the run resolve maps identically by construction.

Correct the data_sources notes: `_REQUIREMENTS` has five entries, not three; `replanning.max_replans` defaults to 0 (not None) and only becomes None when `enabled=True` with the field unset (replanning.py `_promote_unset_budget`); `FailureReason` is a four-value Literal with no `no_progress` bucket, so a NO_PROGRESS termination lands in `stuck` via `_failure_reason`'s fallback (definitions.py:368).

Add an explicit non-citable list to the spec beside the None-valued trap: the un-serialised properties `constraints.n_min_evaluation_episodes`, `robot.t_cycle_ms`, `hardware.ram_budget_breakdown.total_mb`, `environment.sensor_noise.active`, `candidates[i].stack_label`. tool_input.feature: Results-prose drafter for a stored Decision Card — a deterministic, field-cited "results brief" rendered into render_decision_markdown() as a "## Results" section and exposed as JSON, optionally phrased by a model that may not introduce a number.
nonexistent_fields: decision_card.tie_break_reason — CONFIRMED ABSENT. DecisionCard.tie_break_reason is a real model field (card.py:283) but to_json_dict() (card.py:285-325) does not emit it. selection.py:789 sets report['decision_card'] = card.to_json_dict(), and decision_service._store copies that same dict to StoredDecisionRun.card. The spec flagged this correctly; I confirm it, and I confirm the consequence: self_check._rule_tie_break (self_check.py:285-299) cites 'decision_card.tie_break_reason', which resolve() returns None for, so the finding is filtered out at self_check.py:515 and WON_ON_TIE_BREAK is dead in production. tests/test_self_check.py:139-141 (_force_tie_break) hand-builds the key, which is the only place it exists.

alternative.stack — CONFIRMED ABSENT. AlternativeBlock (card.py:129-135) declares exactly candidate_id and reason, model_config extra='forbid'. decision_markdown.py:203 reads alternative.get('stack') and therefore always renders 'not measured'. The spec's bug report is accurate.

manifest.constraints.n_min_evaluation_episodes — CONFIRMED NON-RESOLVING. n_min_evaluation_episodes is an @property on TaskConstraints (task_profile.py:316-323) and manifest.to_json_dict() emits constraints via model_dump() (card.py:425), so the key is absent. sample.n_min_required is the resolvable path (selection.py:617). Spec flagged correctly.

decision_card.gates.G2.statement (dotted, no index) — correctly non-resolving, but see corrections: the spec's risk note overstates this. decision_card.gates[0].G2.statement DOES resolve (verified empirically); resolve() handles the [i] segment. The real hazard is index alignment, not resolvability.

checks[i].<any field> — DOES NOT EXIST. The spec's open question is now answered empirically: report['checks'] is a list of PLAIN STRINGS, not objects. In the stored run they are e.g. 'all 2 candidates still in the run ran the same 6 episode contexts'. There is no code/status/passed field, and a FAILED check is not representable — check_* helpers return a success sentence or raise (selection.py:576-587, consumed as strings at selection.py:862). Nothing under `checks` may be cited except the whole list or `checks[i]` as an opaque string.

manifest.replanning — NOT CITED BY THE SPEC, but a real gap I found: Manifest declares replanning: ReplanningConfig (card.py:378) with a long docstring saying it must be carried, and to_json_dict() (card.py:414-434) omits it. Two runs of one deployment at the same seeds, one replanning and one not, produce byte-identical manifest JSON. Do not cite manifest.replanning; and this is worth raising separately as a HĐ-13 rebuildability bug.

decision_card.preference_profile — does not exist on the card. preference_profile lives on the manifest only (card.py:352, 421). unbuildable_rules: THE STRUCTURAL DEFECT — resolve() cannot distinguish 'key absent' from 'key present with value null'. self_check.resolve() (self_check.py:89-110) returns None in both cases, and critique() filters on `is not None` (self_check.py:515). The spec instructs the new module to 'validate every sentence's field_path through self_check.resolve() before returning it'. That instruction silently DELETES every sentence whose entire reason for existing is that its field is null. Verified empirically against a hand-built ranked card: decision_card.evidence.effect_size, .robustness_margin, .weight_stability_margin, .anchor_stability, decision_card.alternative, decision_card.recommended.params_ref, decision_card.declared_assumptions all returned None while being present-and-null keys. This is not a nitpick: it is the exact failure mode the feature exists to prevent — an unmeasured caveat rendering as silence.

The same applies to weight_stability_margin and anchor_stability whenever the phase-5 sweeps did not run — i.e. every phase-3 run.

    ``local_config``), half need what the registry knows

    candidate became (``candidate_id``, ``observation_requirements``).

    not exist in this particular draft, which is the silent-drop failure
    this whole layer is built to avoid.

    local_config = str(spec.get("local_config", ""))
    params = dict(LOCAL_CONTROLLER_CONFIGS.get(local_config, {}))
    params.update(dict(spec.get("params") or {}))

    info = algorithm_info(stack)
    record: dict[str, Any] = {
        "stack": stack,
        "local_config": local_config,
        "params": params,
        "benchmarkable": getattr(info, "benchmarkable", None),
        "requires_model": getattr(info, "requires_model", None),
        "stochastic_global_planner": getattr(info, "stochastic_global_planner", None),
        "local_controller": getattr(info, "local_controller", None),
        "candidate_id": None,
        "observation_requirements": None,
        "control_period": params.get("control_period"),
        "build_error": None,
    }

        built = candidate_from_stack(stack, params=params)
    except Exception as exc:  # every registry refusal, kept as text
        record["build_error"] = f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"

    map_base_dir: Path | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Assemble the dict the rules read. The only part that touches disk.

    ``profile`` is a ``TaskProfile.model_dump(mode="json")`` and ``specs``
    are the candidate entries from the launch request, so a caller can
    pre-flight exactly the body it is about to POST.

    :func:`~planbench_decision.self_check.critique` takes a report dict:
    the rules stay pure, take one argument, and are testable without a
    filesystem.

    risk = float(constraints.get("collision_probability_max") or 0.0)
    required = _n_min(risk)

            "seed_count": seed_count if seed_count is not None else per_candidate,
            "n_min_required": required,
            "episode_runs_total": per_candidate * len(specs),

    }

    on an unreadable map tells the caller nothing the launch would not
    have told them, and loses the eleven other rules that had nothing to
    do with the map.
    """
    name = str((profile.get("environment") or {}).get("map") or "")
    if not name or base is None:
        return
    try:
        from planbench_benchmark.task_map import load_task_map

        data = load_task_map(name, base_dir=base)
    except Exception as exc:
        draft["map"]["error"] = f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
        return
    draft["map"].update(
        {
            "loaded": True,
            "resolution": getattr(data, "resolution", None),
            "width": getattr(data, "width", None),
            "height": getattr(data, "height", None),
        }
    )


def preflight(draft: Mapping[str, Any]) -> tuple[Advice, ...]:
    """Advice about a comparison that has not run. Never raises.

    Returns an empty tuple for a clean draft. That is a result rather
    than a silence: paired with ``len(PREFLIGHT_CODES)``, it says twelve
    rules looked and none objected, which is the measurement that makes a
    false-alarm rate computable.
    """
    try:
        found = tuple(_rules(draft))
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — advice must never take a caller down
        return ()
    return order(keep_resolvable(found, dict(draft)))


def _rules(draft: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Any:
    profile = dict(draft.get("task_profile") or {})
    candidates = list(draft.get("candidates") or [])
    plan = dict(draft.get("plan") or {})
    environment = dict(profile.get("environment") or {})
    constraints = dict(profile.get("constraints") or {})
    robot = dict(profile.get("robot") or {})

    yield from _candidate_rules(candidates, profile, robot)
    yield from _plan_rules(candidates, plan, constraints)
    yield from _world_rules(candidates, draft, environment, profile)


def _candidate_rules(
    candidates: list[dict[str, Any]], profile: Mapping[str, Any], robot: Mapping[str, Any]
) -> Any:
    available = set(profile.get("available_observations") or ())
    seen: dict[str, int] = {}

    for index, entry in enumerate(candidates):
        stack = entry.get("stack") or "(unnamed)"
        subject = entry.get("candidate_id") or stack

        if entry.get("build_error"):
            yield Advice(
                code="PF_BUILD_FAILED",
                kind="preflight",
                severity="blocking",
                subject=subject,
                claim=f"{stack} cannot be built from the configuration given",
                ground=str(entry["build_error"]),
                field_path=f"candidates[{index}].build_error",
                do="fix the parameter the registry named, or pick a configuration that exists",
                do_not="launch and read the failure as a result about the algorithm",
            )
            continue

        if entry.get("benchmarkable") is False:
            yield Advice(
                code="PF_REFERENCE_STACK_IN_COMPARISON",
                kind="preflight",
                severity="blocking",
                subject=subject,
                claim=f"{stack} is a pipeline reference, not a benchmark entry",
                ground=(
                    "the registry marks it `benchmarkable=False` because it ignores sensing; "
                    "any ranking against it measures the reference's blindness"
                ),
                field_path=f"candidates[{index}].benchmarkable",
                do="compare two benchmarkable stacks, and use the reference only to check the pipeline",
                do_not="report a win over a reference stack as a result about navigation",
            )

        if entry.get("requires_model") and not str(entry.get("params", {}).get("model_id") or ""):
            yield Advice(
                code="PF_MODEL_NOT_CHOSEN",
                kind="preflight",
                severity="blocking",
                subject=subject,
                claim=f"{stack} needs a trained policy and none was named",
                ground="the registry marks it `requires_model=True`; there is no default checkpoint",
                field_path=f"candidates[{index}].requires_model",
                do="name a `model_id` from the model registry",
                do_not="assume a default policy exists — a benchmark must say which one ran",
            )

        required = entry.get("observation_requirements")
        if required is not None and available:
            missing = sorted(set(required) - available)
            if missing:
                yield Advice(
                    code="PF_OBSERVATION_NOT_AVAILABLE",
                    kind="preflight",
                    severity="blocking",
                    subject=subject,
                    claim=f"{stack} needs {', '.join(missing)}, which this deployment does not offer",
                    ground=(
                        "G6 compares the same two lists and will fail this candidate — "
                        "after every episode has run"
                    ),
                    field_path=f"candidates[{index}].observation_requirements",
                    do="declare the observation on the deployment, or choose a stack that fits it",
                    do_not=(
                        "add the token to the deployment just to pass G6 — the deployment is a "
                        "claim about what the robot really has"
                    ),
                )

        period = entry.get("control_period")
        deadline = robot.get("control_period")
        if isinstance(period, (int, float)) and isinstance(deadline, (int, float)):
            if period > deadline:
                yield Advice(
                    code="PF_CONTROL_RATE_SLOWER_THAN_DEPLOYMENT",
                    kind="preflight",
                    severity="material",
                    subject=subject,
                    claim=(
                        f"{stack} is configured to think every {period}s, but the deployment "
                        f"requires a decision every {deadline}s"
                    ),
                    ground="G4 reads the deployment's control period as its deadline",
                    field_path=f"candidates[{index}].control_period",
                    do="lower the controller's control_period, or declare a deployment that can wait",
                    do_not="relax the deployment's control period to make the gate pass",
                )

        if entry.get("stochastic_global_planner"):
            yield Advice(
                code="PF_STOCHASTIC_PLANNER_FEW_SEEDS",
                kind="preflight",
                severity="disclosure",
                subject=subject,
                claim=f"{stack} plans randomly, so one seed is one sample of the planner",
                ground=(
                    "the registry marks it `stochastic_global_planner=True`; its spread across "
                    "seeds is partly its own sampling, not only the deployment's difficulty"
                ),
                field_path=f"candidates[{index}].stochastic_global_planner",
                do="read its numbers across seeds, and say in the report that it is randomised",
                do_not="quote a single seed's path length as the planner's path length",
            )

        cid = entry.get("candidate_id")
        if isinstance(cid, str) and cid:
            if cid in seen:
                yield Advice(
                    code="PF_DUPLICATE_CANDIDATE_ID",
                    kind="preflight",
                    severity="blocking",
                    subject=cid,
                    claim=f"entries {seen[cid]} and {index} are the same configuration",
                    ground=(
                        "`candidate_id` is a hash of the configuration (HĐ-1.3), so these two "
                        "would share every trace, pairing and ΔU"
                    ),
                    field_path=f"candidates[{index}].candidate_id",
                    do="change one of them, or drop it and compare against something different",
                    do_not="read the resulting tie as evidence that two approaches are equivalent",
                )
            else:
                seen[cid] = index


def _plan_rules(
    candidates: list[dict[str, Any]], plan: Mapping[str, Any], constraints: Mapping[str, Any]
) -> Any:
    planned = plan.get("episodes_per_candidate")
    needed = plan.get("n_min_required")
    if isinstance(planned, int) and isinstance(needed, int) and needed > 0 and planned < needed:
        risk = constraints.get("collision_probability_max")
        yield Advice(
            code="PF_EPISODES_BELOW_N_MIN",
            kind="preflight",
            severity="blocking",
            claim=f"{planned} episodes cannot support the declared collision risk",
            ground=(
                f"a claim of at most {risk} needs {needed} clean episodes by the rule of three; "
                "G2 will fail on the count no matter how the runs go"
            ),
            field_path="plan.episodes_per_candidate",
            do=f"run {needed} episodes per candidate, or declare a risk this many episodes can support",
            do_not=(
                "raise collision_probability_max to shrink the requirement — the deployment's "
                "risk is a statement about the world, not a budget"
            ),
        )


def _world_rules(
    candidates: list[dict[str, Any]],
    draft: Mapping[str, Any],
    environment: Mapping[str, Any],
    profile: Mapping[str, Any],
) -> Any:
    traffic = list(environment.get("dynamic_obstacles") or ())
    noise = dict(environment.get("sensor_noise") or {})
    replanning = dict(profile.get("replanning") or {})
    noisy = any(bool(value) for value in noise.values())
    random_planner = any(entry.get("stochastic_global_planner") for entry in candidates)

    if not traffic and not noisy and not random_planner:
        yield Advice(
            code="PF_QUIET_WORLD_REPEATS_ONE_EPISODE",
            kind="preflight",
            severity="material",
            claim="every seed will produce the same episode",
            ground=(
                "no dynamic obstacles, no sensor noise, and no randomised planner — a "
                "deterministic stack replays one trajectory, so N runs carry the information of one"
            ),
            field_path="task_profile.environment.sensor_noise",
            do="add traffic or sensor noise, or state that this measures one trajectory",
            do_not="report a confidence interval over N identical episodes as N samples",
        )

    if traffic and not replanning.get("enabled"):
        yield Advice(
            code="PF_REPLANNING_OFF_WITH_TRAFFIC",
            kind="preflight",
            severity="disclosure",
            claim=f"{len(traffic)} moving obstacles, and a blocked candidate may not replan",
            ground=(
                "replanning is off, so a candidate whose global path is blocked has only its "
                "local controller to escape with"
            ),
            field_path="task_profile.replanning.enabled",
            do="decide this deliberately — both settings are valid experiments",
            do_not=(
                "switch it on midway and compare against earlier runs; it is a different "
                "deployment and needs its own id"
            ),
        )

    map_state = dict(draft.get("map") or {})
    if map_state.get("error"):
        yield Advice(
            code="PF_MAP_UNREADABLE",
            kind="preflight",
            severity="blocking",
            claim="the map this deployment names cannot be read",
            ground=str(map_state["error"]),
            field_path="map.error",
            do="fix the map file or the name the deployment gives it",
            do_not="launch — every candidate would fail for a property of the file",
        )

        built = candidate_from_stack(stack, params=params)
    except Exception as exc:  # every registry refusal, kept as text
        record["build_error"] = f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
        return record

    record["candidate_id"] = built.candidate_id
    record["observation_requirements"] = list(built.observation_requirements)
    return record


def build_draft(
    profile: Mapping[str, Any],
    specs: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]],
    *,
    scope: str = "",
    episodes: int | None = None,
    seed_count: int | None = None,
    map_base_dir: Path | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Assemble the dict the rules read. The only part that touches disk.

    ``profile`` is a ``TaskProfile.model_dump(mode="json")`` and ``specs``
    are the candidate entries from the launch request, so a caller can
    pre-flight exactly the body it is about to POST.

    Separated from :func:`preflight` for the same reason
    :func:`~planbench_decision.self_check.critique` takes a report dict:
    the rules stay pure, take one argument, and are testable without a
    filesystem.
    """
    constraints = dict(profile.get("constraints") or {})
    risk = float(constraints.get("collision_probability_max") or 0.0)
    required = _n_min(risk)
    per_candidate = int(episodes) if episodes else required

    draft: dict[str, Any] = {
        "task_profile": dict(profile),
        "candidates": [_candidate_record(spec) for spec in specs],
        "scope": scope,
        "plan": {
            "episodes_requested": episodes,
            "episodes_per_candidate": per_candidate,
            "seed_count": seed_count if seed_count is not None else per_candidate,
            "n_min_required": required,
            "episode_runs_total": per_candidate * len(specs),
        },
        "map": {"loaded": False, "error": None, "resolution": None},
    }
    _attach_map(draft, profile, map_base_dir)
    return draft


def _attach_map(draft: dict[str, Any], profile: Mapping[str, Any], base: Path | None) -> None:
    """Load the map named by the profile, or record why it could not be.

    A failure here is advice, not an exception: a pre-flight that raises
    on an unreadable map tells the caller nothing the launch would not
    have told them, and loses the eleven other rules that had nothing to
    do with the map.
    """
    name = str((profile.get("environment") or {}).get("map") or "")
    if not name or base is None:
        return
    try:
        from planbench_benchmark.task_map import load_task_map

        data = load_task_map(name, base_dir=base)
    except Exception as exc:
        draft["map"]["error"] = f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
        return
    draft["map"].update(
        {
            "loaded": True,
            "resolution": getattr(data, "resolution", None),
            "width": getattr(data, "width", None),
            "height": getattr(data, "height", None),
        }
    )


def preflight(draft: Mapping[str, Any]) -> tuple[Advice, ...]:
    """Advice about a comparison that has not run. Never raises.

    Returns an empty tuple for a clean draft. That is a result rather
    than a silence: paired with ``len(PREFLIGHT_CODES)``, it says twelve
    rules looked and none objected, which is the measurement that makes a
    false-alarm rate computable.
    """
    try:
        found = tuple(_rules(draft))
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — advice must never take a caller down
        return ()
    return order(keep_resolvable(found, dict(draft)))


def _rules(draft: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Any:
    profile = dict(draft.get("task_profile") or {})
    candidates = list(draft.get("candidates") or [])
    plan = dict(draft.get("plan") or {})
    environment = dict(profile.get("environment") or {})
    constraints = dict(profile.get("constraints") or {})
    robot = dict(profile.get("robot") or {})

    yield from _candidate_rules(candidates, profile, robot)
    yield from _plan_rules(candidates, plan, constraints)
    yield from _world_rules(candidates, draft, environment, profile)


def _candidate_rules(
    candidates: list[dict[str, Any]], profile: Mapping[str, Any], robot: Mapping[str, Any]
) -> Any:
    available = set(profile.get("available_observations") or ())
    seen: dict[str, int] = {}

    for index, entry in enumerate(candidates):
        stack = entry.get("stack") or "(unnamed)"
        subject = entry.get("candidate_id") or stack

        if entry.get("build_error"):
            yield Advice(
                code="PF_BUILD_FAILED",
                kind="preflight",
                severity="blocking",
                subject=subject,
                claim=f"{stack} cannot be built from the configuration given",
                ground=str(entry["build_error"]),
                field_path=f"candidates[{index}].build_error",
                do="fix the parameter the registry named, or pick a configuration that exists",
                do_not="launch and read the failure as a result about the algorithm",
            )
            continue

        if entry.get("benchmarkable") is False:
            yield Advice(
                code="PF_REFERENCE_STACK_IN_COMPARISON",
                kind="preflight",
                severity="blocking",
                subject=subject,
                claim=f"{stack} is a pipeline reference, not a benchmark entry",
                ground=(
                    "the registry marks it `benchmarkable=False` because it ignores sensing; "
                    "any ranking against it measures the reference's blindness"
                ),
                field_path=f"candidates[{index}].benchmarkable",
                do="compare two benchmarkable stacks, and use the reference only to check the pipeline",
                do_not="report a win over a reference stack as a result about navigation",
            )

        if entry.get("requires_model") and not str(entry.get("params", {}).get("model_id") or ""):
            yield Advice(
                code="PF_MODEL_NOT_CHOSEN",
                kind="preflight",
                severity="blocking",
                subject=subject,
                claim=f"{stack} needs a trained policy and none was named",
                ground="the registry marks it `requires_model=True`; there is no default checkpoint",
                field_path=f"candidates[{index}].requires_model",
                do="name a `model_id` from the model registry",
                do_not="assume a default policy exists — a benchmark must say which one ran",
            )

        required = entry.get("observation_requirements")
        if required is not None and available:
            missing = sorted(set(required) - available)
            if missing:
                yield Advice(
                    code="PF_OBSERVATION_NOT_AVAILABLE",
                    kind="preflight",
                    severity="blocking",
                    subject=subject,
                    claim=f"{stack} needs {', '.join(missing)}, which this deployment does not offer",
                    ground=(
                        "G6 compares the same two lists and will fail this candidate — "
                        "after every episode has run"
                    ),
                    field_path=f"candidates[{index}].observation_requirements",
                    do="declare the observation on the deployment, or choose a stack that fits it",
                    do_not=(
                        "add the token to the deployment just to pass G6 — the deployment is a "
                        "claim about what the robot really has"
                    ),
                )

        period = entry.get("control_period")
        deadline = robot.get("control_period")
        if isinstance(period, (int, float)) and isinstance(deadline, (int, float)):
            if period > deadline:
                yield Advice(
                    code="PF_CONTROL_RATE_SLOWER_THAN_DEPLOYMENT",
                    kind="preflight",
                    severity="material",
                    subject=subject,
                    claim=(
                        f"{stack} is configured to think every {period}s, but the deployment "
                        f"requires a decision every {deadline}s"
                    ),
                    ground="G4 reads the deployment's control period as its deadline",
                    field_path=f"candidates[{index}].control_period",
                    do="lower the controller's control_period, or declare a deployment that can wait",
                    do_not="relax the deployment's control period to make the gate pass",
                )

        if entry.get("stochastic_global_planner"):
            yield Advice(
                code="PF_STOCHASTIC_PLANNER_FEW_SEEDS",
                kind="preflight",
                severity="disclosure",
                subject=subject,
                claim=f"{stack} plans randomly, so one seed is one sample of the planner",
                ground=(
                    "the registry marks it `stochastic_global_planner=True`; its spread across "
                    "seeds is partly its own sampling, not only the deployment's difficulty"
                ),
                field_path=f"candidates[{index}].stochastic_global_planner",
                do="read its numbers across seeds, and say in the report that it is randomised",
                do_not="quote a single seed's path length as the planner's path length",
            )

        cid = entry.get("candidate_id")
        if isinstance(cid, str) and cid:
            if cid in seen:
                yield Advice(
                    code="PF_DUPLICATE_CANDIDATE_ID",
                    kind="preflight",
                    severity="blocking",
                    subject=cid,
                    claim=f"entries {seen[cid]} and {index} are the same configuration",
                    ground=(
                        "`candidate_id` is a hash of the configuration (HĐ-1.3), so these two "
                        "would share every trace, pairing and ΔU"
                    ),
                    field_path=f"candidates[{index}].candidate_id",
                    do="change one of them, or drop it and compare against something different",
                    do_not="read the resulting tie as evidence that two approaches are equivalent",
                )
            else:
                seen[cid] = index


def _plan_rules(
    candidates: list[dict[str, Any]], plan: Mapping[str, Any], constraints: Mapping[str, Any]
) -> Any:
    planned = plan.get("episodes_per_candidate")
    needed = plan.get("n_min_required")
    if isinstance(planned, int) and isinstance(needed, int) and needed > 0 and planned < needed:
        risk = constraints.get("collision_probability_max")
        yield Advice(
            code="PF_EPISODES_BELOW_N_MIN",
            kind="preflight",
            severity="blocking",
            claim=f"{planned} episodes cannot support the declared collision risk",
            ground=(
                f"a claim of at most {risk} needs {needed} clean episodes by the rule of three; "
                "G2 will fail on the count no matter how the runs go"
            ),
            field_path="plan.episodes_per_candidate",
            do=f"run {needed} episodes per candidate, or declare a risk this many episodes can support",
            do_not=(
                "raise collision_probability_max to shrink the requirement — the deployment's "
                "risk is a statement about the world, not a budget"
            ),
        )


def _world_rules(
    candidates: list[dict[str, Any]],
    draft: Mapping[str, Any],
    environment: Mapping[str, Any],
    profile: Mapping[str, Any],
) -> Any:
    traffic = list(environment.get("dynamic_obstacles") or ())
    noise = dict(environment.get("sensor_noise") or {})
    replanning = dict(profile.get("replanning") or {})
    noisy = any(bool(value) for value in noise.values())
    random_planner = any(entry.get("stochastic_global_planner") for entry in candidates)

    if not traffic and not noisy and not random_planner:
        yield Advice(
            code="PF_QUIET_WORLD_REPEATS_ONE_EPISODE",
            kind="preflight",
            severity="material",
            claim="every seed will produce the same episode",
            ground=(
                "no dynamic obstacles, no sensor noise, and no randomised planner — a "
                "deterministic stack replays one trajectory, so N runs carry the information of one"
            ),
            field_path="task_profile.environment.sensor_noise",
            do="add traffic or sensor noise, or state that this measures one trajectory",
            do_not="report a confidence interval over N identical episodes as N samples",
        )

    if traffic and not replanning.get("enabled"):
        yield Advice(
            code="PF_REPLANNING_OFF_WITH_TRAFFIC",
            kind="preflight",
            severity="disclosure",
            claim=f"{len(traffic)} moving obstacles, and a blocked candidate may not replan",
            ground=(
                "replanning is off, so a candidate whose global path is blocked has only its "
                "local controller to escape with"
            ),
            field_path="task_profile.replanning.enabled",
            do="decide this deliberately — both settings are valid experiments",
            do_not=(
                "switch it on midway and compare against earlier runs; it is a different "
                "deployment and needs its own id"
            ),
        )

    map_state = dict(draft.get("map") or {})
    if map_state.get("error"):
        yield Advice(
            code="PF_MAP_UNREADABLE",
            kind="preflight",
            severity="blocking",
            claim="the map this deployment names cannot be read",
            ground=str(map_state["error"]),
            field_path="map.error",
            do="fix the map file or the name the deployment gives it",
            do_not="launch — every candidate would fail for a property of the file",
        )

"""Turn a failed gate into a next step, and name the step that is barred.

A gate table says ``G3: fail``. True, checkable, and it leaves the reader
to work out alone whether the answer is a better candidate, a different
scenario split, or the one move that makes the symptom vanish without
making the conclusion true: edit ``success_rate_min`` down and run again.

That move is one field away in a form the same person is authorised to
edit. Every gate here has one like it — loosen the threshold, widen the
collision risk so ``N_min`` shrinks, declare an observation token the
robot does not really carry — and a reader told only "this failed" is
being invited to go looking.

So each piece of advice carries both halves. ``do`` is the legitimate
route; ``do_not`` names the barred one explicitly, because leaving it
implicit is how it gets taken. The report already says this once, in
``why_no_card``, for the run as a whole: *"the valid way out is to
register a new candidate, not to loosen the deployment"*. This module
says it per candidate and per gate, where the reader is actually looking.

**Two sources, one dict.** A gate's threshold lives on the task profile
and its observation lives on the report — ``G3: "fail"`` is a bare string
with no number in it. :func:`build_diagnosis` merges them under
``report.`` and ``task_profile.`` so every citation resolves against one
object, the way ``keep_resolvable`` requires.

**It never re-decides.** The verdicts are read, never recomputed. A
module that could disagree with a gate would be a second gate with no
contract behind it.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Mapping
from typing import Any

from planbench_decision.advice import Advice, keep_resolvable, order

__all__ = [
    "GATE_ADVICE_CODES",
    "build_diagnosis",
    "gate_advice",
]

GATE_ADVICE_CODES: tuple[str, ...] = (
    "GA_G1_NO_PATH",
    "GA_G2_COLLISION",
    "GA_G2_TOO_FEW_EPISODES",
    "GA_G3_SUCCESS_RATE",
    "GA_G4_TOO_SLOW",
    "GA_G4_HOST_ONLY",
    "GA_G5_MEMORY",
    "GA_G6_OBSERVATION",
    "GA_NOBODY_CLEARED",
    "GA_UNPINNED_MEASUREMENT",
)

#: Gate verdicts that mean "did not pass". Read rather than recomputed —
#: this module explains gates, it does not get a vote.
_FAILED = {"fail", "failed", "blocked"}


def build_diagnosis(
    report: Mapping[str, Any], profile: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """One dict holding both halves of the evidence.

    The report says what happened; the task profile says what was
    required. ``G3: "fail"`` carries neither the rate observed nor the
    rate demanded, so advice that named only one of them would be advice
    a reader could not check.
    """
    return {"report": dict(report), "task_profile": dict(profile or {})}


def gate_advice(diagnosis: Mapping[str, Any]) -> tuple[Advice, ...]:
    """Advice for every gate a candidate did not clear. Never raises."""
    try:
        found = tuple(_rules(diagnosis))
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — advice must never take a caller down
        return ()
    return order(keep_resolvable(found, dict(diagnosis)))


def _verdict(gate: Any) -> str:
    """The verdict, whichever shape this gate reports in.

    G1, G3 and G6 are bare strings; G2, G4 and G5 are dicts with a
    ``result`` key. A caller that assumed one shape would silently skip
    half the gates.
    """
    if isinstance(gate, str):
        return gate
    if isinstance(gate, dict):
        return str(gate.get("result", ""))
    return ""


def _rules(diagnosis: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Any:
    report = dict(diagnosis.get("report") or {})
    profile = dict(diagnosis.get("task_profile") or {})
    constraints = dict(profile.get("constraints") or {})
    candidates = list(report.get("candidates") or [])

    for index, entry in enumerate(candidates):
        gates = dict(entry.get("gates") or {})
        label = entry.get("stack_label") or entry.get("candidate_id") or f"entry {index}"
        subject = str(entry.get("candidate_id") or label)
        at = f"report.candidates[{index}]"

        yield from _g1(gates, constraints, entry, label, subject, at)
        yield from _g2(gates, label, subject, at)
        yield from _g3(gates, constraints, entry, label, subject, at)
        yield from _g4(gates, label, subject, at)
        yield from _g5(gates, label, subject, at)
        yield from _g6(gates, label, subject, at)

    yield from _run_rules(report, candidates)


def _g1(
    gates: Mapping[str, Any],
    constraints: Mapping[str, Any],
    entry: Mapping[str, Any],
    label: str,
    subject: str,
    at: str,
) -> Any:
    if _verdict(gates.get("G1")) not in _FAILED:
        return
    allowed = constraints.get("no_path_rate_max")
    yield Advice(
        code="GA_G1_NO_PATH",
        kind="diagnosis",
        severity="blocking",
        subject=subject,
        claim=f"{label} failed to find a path more often than this deployment allows",
        ground=(
            f"G1 compares the no-path rate against no_path_rate_max"
            f"{f' = {allowed}' if allowed is not None else ''}; a planner that returns no path "
            "never reaches the controller, so nothing downstream is measured"
        ),
        field_path=f"{at}.gates.G1",
        do=(
            "check the missions actually fit the map for this robot radius, then try a "
            "planner that searches harder — this is usually geometry, not tuning"
        ),
        do_not=(
            "raise no_path_rate_max so the gate passes; the rate is what the deployment "
            "can tolerate, not what this candidate happened to achieve"
        ),
    )


def _g2(gates: Mapping[str, Any], label: str, subject: str, at: str) -> Any:
    gate = gates.get("G2")
    if not isinstance(gate, dict) or _verdict(gate) not in _FAILED:
        return
    observed = gate.get("observed")
    n_runs = gate.get("n_distinct_episodes") or gate.get("n_runs")
    n_min = gate.get("n_min")

    if isinstance(observed, int) and observed > 0:
        yield Advice(
            code="GA_G2_COLLISION",
            kind="diagnosis",
            severity="blocking",
            subject=subject,
            claim=f"{label} collided {observed} time(s)",
            ground=(
                "G2 requires zero collisions over the evaluation set; one is enough to fail "
                "it, because the claim being made is about safety and not about an average"
            ),
            field_path=f"{at}.gates.G2.observed",
            do=(
                "open the trace for a colliding episode and read what the clearance did "
                "before impact; raise safety_margin if the controller cut it fine"
            ),
            do_not=(
                "average the collisions away over more episodes — the gate is a zero, "
                "not a rate"
            ),
        )

    if isinstance(n_runs, int) and isinstance(n_min, int) and n_runs < n_min:
        yield Advice(
            code="GA_G2_TOO_FEW_EPISODES",
            kind="diagnosis",
            severity="blocking",
            subject=subject,
            claim=f"{n_runs} clean episodes cannot support the declared collision risk",
            ground=(
                f"the rule of three needs {n_min} for this deployment's declared risk; "
                "zero collisions in too few runs is not evidence of safety"
            ),
            field_path=f"{at}.gates.G2.n_min",
            do=f"run at least {n_min} episodes per candidate",
            do_not=(
                "raise collision_probability_max to shrink N_min — the declared risk is a "
                "statement about the world, not a budget for compute"
            ),
        )


def _g3(
    gates: Mapping[str, Any],
    constraints: Mapping[str, Any],
    entry: Mapping[str, Any],
    label: str,
    subject: str,
    at: str,
) -> Any:
    if _verdict(gates.get("G3")) not in _FAILED:
        return
    rate = entry.get("success_rate")
    threshold = constraints.get("success_rate_min")
    seen = f"{rate:.0%}" if isinstance(rate, (int, float)) else "its success rate"
    wanted = f" against {threshold:.0%} required" if isinstance(threshold, (int, float)) else ""
    yield Advice(
        code="GA_G3_SUCCESS_RATE",
        kind="diagnosis",

A gate table says ``G3: fail``. True, checkable, and it leaves the reader
to work out alone whether the answer is a better candidate, a different
scenario split, or the one move that makes the symptom vanish without
making the conclusion true: edit ``success_rate_min`` down and run again.

That move is one field away in a form the same person is authorised to
edit. Every gate here has one like it — loosen the threshold, widen the
collision risk so ``N_min`` shrinks, declare an observation token the
robot does not really carry — and a reader told only "this failed" is
being invited to go looking.

So each piece of advice carries both halves. ``do`` is the legitimate
route; ``do_not`` names the barred one explicitly, because leaving it
implicit is how it gets taken. The report already says this once, in
``why_no_card``, for the run as a whole: *"the valid way out is to
register a new candidate, not to loosen the deployment"*. This module
says it per candidate and per gate, where the reader is actually looking.

**Two sources, one dict.** A gate's threshold lives on the task profile
and its observation lives on the report — ``G3: "fail"`` is a bare string
with no number in it. :func:`build_diagnosis` merges them under
``report.`` and ``task_profile.`` so every citation resolves against one
object, the way ``keep_resolvable`` requires.

**It never re-decides.** The verdicts are read, never recomputed. A
module that could disagree with a gate would be a second gate with no
contract behind it.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping
from typing import Any

from planbench_decision.advice import Advice, keep_resolvable, order

__all__ = [
    "GATE_ADVICE_CODES",
    "build_diagnosis",
    "gate_advice",
]

GATE_ADVICE_CODES: tuple[str, ...] = (
    "GA_G1_NO_PATH",
    "GA_G2_COLLISION",
    "GA_G2_TOO_FEW_EPISODES",
    "GA_G3_SUCCESS_RATE",
    "GA_G4_TOO_SLOW",
    "GA_G4_HOST_ONLY",
    "GA_G5_MEMORY",
    "GA_G6_OBSERVATION",
    "GA_NOBODY_CLEARED",
    "GA_UNPINNED_MEASUREMENT",
)
