    "OC_TRAIT_SURPRISE",
    "OC_WINNER_ON_MARGIN",
)

#: What each algorithm family is known for. ``anchor`` says where the
#: claim can be checked: a registry flag, or the algorithm's defining
#: mechanics. Nothing here is a measurement — measurements come from the
#: report, and the rules only pair the two.
TRAITS: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {
    "astar": {
        "kind": "global",
        "strengths": (
            "complete and optimal on the grid it searches — the same map in gives the same path out",
            "cost is bounded by the grid, so latency is predictable episode to episode",
        ),
        "weaknesses": (
            "paths are grid-constrained: never shorter than the 8-connected lattice allows",
            "search cost grows with map size and inflation, all of it paid before the robot moves",
        ),
        "anchor": "deterministic by construction; registry marks stochastic_global_planner=False",
    },
    "rrtstar": {
        "kind": "global",
        "strengths": (
            "any-angle paths — sampling is not bound to a lattice, so converged paths run shorter",
            "anytime: more iterations buy a better tree without a new algorithm",
        ),
        "weaknesses": (
            "stochastic: one seed is one draw, and its spread across seeds is its own sampling noise",
            "tail latency is the price of sampling — the slowest episodes are where the tree grew wrong",
        ),
        "anchor": "registry marks stochastic_global_planner=True; results must be read across seeds",
    },
    "dwa": {
        "kind": "local",
        "strengths": (
            "reactive and cheap per tick: samples reachable velocities against the live costmap",
            "degrades gracefully — a blocked rollout costs a bad score, not a crash",
        ),
        "weaknesses": (
            "local: it optimises one horizon, so doorways and dead ends it cannot see past become stalls",
            "oscillation-prone in tight spaces — competing rollouts flip the turn direction",
        ),
        "anchor": "velocity-sampling controller; horizon and weights are its whole world",
    },
    "ppo": {
        "kind": "local",
        "strengths": ("learned reactions can beat hand-tuned costs inside the training distribution",),
        "weaknesses": (
            "behaviour is bound to the training distribution; a new map is an out-of-distribution question",
            "needs a named checkpoint — the number means nothing without which policy produced it",
        ),
        "anchor": "registry marks requires_model=True",
    },
    "pure_pursuit": {
        "kind": "local",
        "strengths": ("a pipeline reference: follows the path and nothing else",),
        "weaknesses": ("ignores sensing entirely, so any ranking against it measures its blindness",),
        "anchor": "registry marks benchmarkable=False",
    },
}


def _components(stack_label: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """``astar+dwa`` → its two component names, from the registry when it
    knows the stack, from the label's own shape when it does not."""
    info = algorithm_info(stack_label)
    if info is not None:
        return str(info.global_planner), str(info.local_controller)
    left, _, right = str(stack_label).partition("+")
    return left, right


def build_outcome(
    report: Mapping[str, Any], profile: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """One dict: the report, each candidate's traits, and the deployment.

    The traits ride inside the source rather than being looked up by the
    rules, for the same reason every module in this family pre-computes
    its diff: each rule cites a path into the structure the caller can
    render, and a citation into a table the reader cannot see would be
    advice they cannot check.
    """
    candidates = []
    for entry in report.get("candidates") or []:
        stack = str(entry.get("stack_label") or "")
        global_name, local_name = _components(stack)
        candidates.append(
            {
                **dict(entry),
                "global_planner": global_name,
                "local_controller": local_name,
                "traits": {
                    "global": TRAITS.get(global_name, {}),
                    "local": TRAITS.get(local_name, {}),
                },
            }
        )
    return {
        "report": {**dict(report), "candidates": candidates},
        "task_profile": dict(profile or {}),
    }


def outcome_advice(source: Mapping[str, Any]) -> tuple[Advice, ...]:
    """Why the run ended the way it did. Never raises."""
    try:
        found = tuple(_rules(source))
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — advice must never take a caller down
        return ()
    return order(keep_resolvable(found, dict(source)))


def _rules(source: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Any:
    report = dict(source.get("report") or {})
    candidates = list(report.get("candidates") or [])
    card = report.get("decision_card")

    yield from _gate_eliminations(candidates)
    yield from _scope_isolation(report, candidates)
    if isinstance(card, dict):
        yield from _card_rules(card, candidates)
    yield from _metric_rules(candidates)


def _gate_eliminations(candidates: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> Any:
    """A loss at the gates is a different kind of loss, and the trait
    that predicts it is worth naming next to the number."""
    for index, entry in enumerate(candidates):
        blocking = list(entry.get("blocking_gates") or [])
        if not blocking:
            continue
        label = entry.get("stack_label") or entry.get("candidate_id") or f"entry {index}"
        weaknesses = tuple((entry.get("traits") or {}).get("local", {}).get("weaknesses") or ())
        nature = f" {label.split('+')[-1]}'s known weakness — {weaknesses[0]} — is the first place to look." if weaknesses else ""
        yield Advice(
            code="OC_ELIMINATED_BY_GATE",
            kind="diagnosis",
            severity="material",
            subject=str(entry.get("candidate_id") or label),
            claim=f"{label} did not lose the ranking — it was eliminated at {', '.join(blocking)}",
            ground=(
                "an eliminated candidate never entered the ΔU comparison, so the outcome is "
                f"a gate story, not a margin story.{nature}"
            ),
            field_path=f"report.candidates[{index}].blocking_gates",
            do=(
                "read the failed gate's advice and the failing episodes' traces before "
                "concluding anything about the algorithm itself"
            ),
            do_not=(
                "describe this as the other stack 'winning' — nobody was compared; one "
                "entry did not qualify"
            ),
        )


def _scope_isolation(report: Mapping[str, Any], candidates: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> Any:
    """When both candidates share a local controller, the outcome is
    about the global planners — a fact the scope declares and readers
    routinely miss."""
    if len(candidates) < 2:
        return
    locals_ = {entry.get("local_controller") for entry in candidates}
    scope = (report.get("identity") or {}).get("experiment_scope")
    if len(locals_) == 1 and scope == "global_planner_selection":
        globals_ = " vs ".join(str(entry.get("global_planner")) for entry in candidates[:2])
        yield Advice(
            code="OC_SAME_CONTROLLER_ISOLATES_PLANNER",
            kind="diagnosis",
            severity="disclosure",
            claim=f"both candidates drive with the same controller, so this outcome is {globals_}",
            ground=(
                "the experiment scope holds the local layer fixed; every difference in the "
                "numbers is attributable to the global planners and their interaction with it"
            ),
            field_path="report.identity.experiment_scope",
            do="read the result as a planner comparison, which is what the scope was built to isolate",
            do_not="credit the controller for a gap the scope deliberately kept it out of",
        )


def _card_rules(card: dict[str, Any], candidates: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> Any:
    status = str(card.get("status") or "")
    evidence = dict(card.get("evidence") or {})
    recommended = dict(card.get("recommended") or {})
    winner_stack = str(recommended.get("stack") or "")
    ci = evidence.get("ci95")
    delta = evidence.get("delta_u_vs_second")

    if status == "NEAR_EQUIVALENT" or (
        isinstance(ci, (list, tuple)) and len(ci) == 2 and ci[0] <= 0.0 <= ci[1]
    ):
        yield Advice(
            code="OC_MARGIN_IS_NOISE",
            kind="diagnosis",
            severity="material",
            subject=str(recommended.get("candidate_id") or ""),
            claim="the margin between these candidates does not clear the noise",
            ground=(
                f"ΔU {delta} with CI95 {ci}: an interval that touches zero means the sign of "
                "the difference is not established, whatever the point estimate says"
            ),
            field_path="report.decision_card.evidence.ci95",
            do=(
                "say 'no established difference on this deployment' — that is a result, and "
                "often the useful one"
            ),
            do_not="name a winner from a point estimate whose interval contains zero",
        )
        return

    if winner_stack:
        global_name, _, _rest = winner_stack.partition("+")
        trait = TRAITS.get(global_name, {})
        strengths = tuple(trait.get("strengths") or ())
        nature = f" That is what {global_name} is built for: {strengths[0]}." if strengths else ""
        yield Advice(
            code="OC_WINNER_ON_MARGIN",
            kind="diagnosis",
            severity="disclosure",
            subject=str(recommended.get("candidate_id") or ""),
            claim=f"{winner_stack} won on a margin the interval supports",
            ground=(
                f"ΔU {delta}, CI95 {ci}, over {evidence.get('n_episodes')} paired episodes."
                f"{nature}"
            ),
            field_path="report.decision_card.evidence.delta_u_vs_second",
            do="quote the margin with its interval and episode count, never the point alone",
            do_not=(
                "generalise past this deployment — the margin was measured on one map, one "
                "robot, one mission set"
            ),
        )


def _metric_rules(candidates: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> Any:
    """Which observable metric actually separated the field, tied to the
    trait that predicts it — or flagged when the trait predicts the
    opposite."""
    measured = [
        (index, entry)
        for index, entry in enumerate(candidates)
        if isinstance(entry.get("success_rate"), (int, float))
    ]
    if len(measured) < 2:
        return
    (index_a, a), (index_b, b) = measured[0], measured[1]

    gap = float(a["success_rate"]) - float(b["success_rate"])
    if abs(gap) >= 0.1:
        lead, trail = (a, b) if gap > 0 else (b, a)
        lead_index = index_a if gap > 0 else index_b
        yield Advice(
            code="OC_METRIC_DRIVER",
            kind="diagnosis",
            severity="disclosure",
            subject=str(lead.get("candidate_id") or ""),
            claim=(
                f"success rate is the separator: {lead.get('stack_label')} "
                f"{lead.get('success_rate'):.0%} against {trail.get('stack_label')} "
                f"{trail.get('success_rate'):.0%}"
            ),
            ground=(
                "a gap this wide is about episodes one stack finishes and the other does "
                "not — read the failing episodes' termination reasons before crediting speed "
                "or path quality"
            ),
            field_path=f"report.candidates[{lead_index}].success_rate",
            do="open the trailing stack's failed traces; the reason (stall, timeout, no-path) names the fix",
            do_not="attribute a success-rate gap to path optimality — finishing is upstream of quality",
        )

    lat_a, lat_b = a.get("pooled_p99_latency_ms"), b.get("pooled_p99_latency_ms")
    if isinstance(lat_a, (int, float)) and isinstance(lat_b, (int, float)) and min(lat_a, lat_b) > 0:
        slow_index, slow = (index_a, a) if lat_a >= lat_b else (index_b, b)
        fast = b if lat_a >= lat_b else a
        ratio = max(lat_a, lat_b) / min(lat_a, lat_b)
        if ratio >= 2.0:
            stochastic = bool(
                (slow.get("traits") or {}).get("global", {}).get("anchor", "").find("stochastic_global_planner=True") >= 0
            )
            if stochastic:
                yield Advice(
                    code="OC_LATENCY_PRICE_OF_SAMPLING",
                    kind="diagnosis",
                    severity="disclosure",
                    subject=str(slow.get("candidate_id") or ""),
                    claim=(
                        f"{slow.get('stack_label')} pays {ratio:.1f}x the tail latency of "
                        f"{fast.get('stack_label')}, and its own nature predicts that"
                    ),
                    ground=(
                        "the registry marks its global planner stochastic; tail latency is the "
                        "textbook price of sampling — the slowest episodes are where the tree "
                        "grew wrong before it grew right"
                    ),
                    field_path=f"report.candidates[{slow_index}].pooled_p99_latency_ms",
                    do=(
                        "treat the tail as inherent, not as a tuning bug: cap iterations if the "
                        "deadline matters more than path quality"
                    ),
                    do_not="tune expecting deterministic-planner latency from a sampling planner",
                )
            else:
                yield Advice(
                    code="OC_TRAIT_SURPRISE",
                    kind="diagnosis",
                    severity="material",
                    subject=str(slow.get("candidate_id") or ""),
                    claim=(
                        f"{slow.get('stack_label')} is {ratio:.1f}x slower at p99 than "
                        f"{fast.get('stack_label')}, and nothing in its nature predicts that"
                    ),
                    ground=(
                        "its global planner is deterministic, whose latency should be bounded "
                        "by the grid; a tail this long on a deterministic stack usually means "
                        "an oversized search space or replans nobody counted on"
                    ),
                    field_path=f"report.candidates[{slow_index}].pooled_p99_latency_ms",
                    do="check the map inflation and the replan rows before blaming the algorithm",
                    do_not="accept a surprising number because it favours the expected winner",
                )

class TestAPaperCanActuallyBeRegistered:
    """The end-user test that found the identity split.

    The paper reading prints a candidate_id computed from the stated
    parameters; the registration form only accepted a *named* config, so
    that id could never be registered — the diff button 404'd for a user
    who did everything right. Registration now takes explicit params,
    through the same hash path, so the id the reading printed is the id
    the registration returns.
    """

    EXTRACTION_PARAMS = {
        "control_period": 0.1,
        "horizon_seconds": 1.5,
        "velocity_samples": 7,
        "omega_samples": 15,
    }

    def test_registering_the_papers_params_yields_the_papers_id(self, client, alice_headers):
        from planbench_benchmark.candidates import candidate_from_stack

        expected = candidate_from_stack("rrtstar+dwa", params=dict(self.EXTRACTION_PARAMS))
        response = client.post(
            "/api/v1/candidates",
            json={"stack": "rrtstar+dwa", "params": self.EXTRACTION_PARAMS},
            headers=alice_headers,
        )
        assert response.status_code in (200, 201), response.text
        assert response.json()["candidate_id"] == expected.candidate_id

    def test_a_name_and_params_together_are_refused_out_loud(self, client, alice_headers):
        """With both, which one defines the candidate would be the
        server's private decision — and a private decision about
        identity is an identity bug waiting to be filed."""
        response = client.post(
            "/api/v1/candidates",
            json={
                "stack": "rrtstar+dwa",
                "local_config": "dwa_coarse",
                "params": self.EXTRACTION_PARAMS,
            },
            headers=alice_headers,
        )
        assert response.status_code == 422
        assert "not both" in response.text

    def test_an_unknown_parameter_is_refused_not_ignored(self, client, alice_headers):
        response = client.post(
            "/api/v1/candidates",
            json={"stack": "rrtstar+dwa", "params": {"no_such_knob": 1}},
            headers=alice_headers,
        )
        assert response.status_code == 422

    def test_the_bare_registration_still_defaults_to_dwa_coarse(self, client, alice_headers):
        """Every existing caller sends only a stack name; that door must
        not have moved."""
        response = client.post(
            "/api/v1/candidates", json={"stack": "astar+dwa"}, headers=alice_headers
        )
        assert response.status_code in (200, 201), response.text

"""Tell a reader what to do next, and what not to do.

Every gate in this codebase answers pass or fail. That is the right shape
for a decision and the wrong shape for a person: "G3 fail, 0.71 < 0.85"
is true, checkable, and leaves the reader to work out on their own
whether the fix is a better candidate, a different scenario split, or —
the move that quietly destroys the whole point — a looser threshold.

This module is the shape for the second half. An :class:`Advice` is a
:class:`~planbench_decision.self_check.Finding` with two more fields:
what a reader can legitimately do, and what they must not. The second
one is the one that earns the module. Every gate in this platform has an
illegitimate remedy that makes it pass, most of them are one edit away,
and a reader who was told only "this failed" is being invited to find
them.

Three rules, inherited from :mod:`planbench_decision.self_check` and
extended by one:

**Every piece of advice cites a field that exists.** ``field_path``
resolves against the source data through
:func:`~planbench_decision.self_check.resolve`. Advice that cannot point
at its own evidence reads as verified and is not, and the same check is
what keeps an LLM layer honest — it may rank and rephrase, it may not
invent a citation.

**Advice never acts.** These objects are text. Nothing here launches a
run, edits a deployment or approves a result; those are human acts on
the decisions page, and the agent's published
``FORBIDDEN_CAPABILITIES`` says so where a caller can check it.

**A forbidden remedy is named, not implied.** ``do_not`` is empty only
when there genuinely is no tempting wrong move. Leaving it empty because
the wrong move is "obvious" is how it gets taken.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any, Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict

from planbench_decision.self_check import Severity, resolve

__all__ = [
    "Advice",
    "AdviceKind",
    "Severity",
    "keep_resolvable",
    "order",
    "resolve",
]

#: Which half of the lifecycle a piece of advice belongs to. Carried so a
#: caller can render "before you spend the compute" separately from
#: "now that you have the numbers" without parsing the code strings.
AdviceKind = Literal["preflight", "diagnosis", "reproduction", "reporting"]

#: Severity ordering used for display. `blocking` first, because a reader
#: who stops after the first line should have read the one that changes
#: what they do next.
_SEVERITY_RANK: dict[str, int] = {"blocking": 0, "material": 1, "disclosure": 2}


class Advice(BaseModel):
    """One thing a reader should do, grounded in one field they can check."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    #: Stable identifier. Lets a rule be tracked across runs, scored by an
    #: evaluation harness, and silenced by a reader who disagrees with it
    #: without silencing everything.
    code: str
    kind: AdviceKind
    severity: Severity
    #: The situation, stated as something checkable against `field_path`.
    claim: str
    #: Why it is the case, in one sentence. Not persuasion — the sentence
    #: a reader compares against the field to decide whether to believe
    #: the advice at all.
    ground: str
    #: Dotted path into the source data. Always resolvable; see
    #: :func:`keep_resolvable`, which is what enforces it.
    field_path: str
    #: The legitimate next step. Concrete enough to act on: "register a
    #: candidate with a smaller lookahead" rather than "improve the
    #: configuration".
    do: str
    #: The move that would make the symptom disappear without making the
    #: conclusion true. Empty only when there is genuinely no such move.
    do_not: str = ""


def keep_resolvable(items: tuple[Advice, ...], source: dict[str, Any]) -> tuple[Advice, ...]:
    """Drop advice whose ``field_path`` does not resolve against ``source``.

    Applied to rule output as well as model output, deliberately. A rule
    that points at a field a particular report happens not to carry is
    making the same unverifiable claim a hallucinating model would, and
    the reader has no way to tell the two apart. Better to lose the
    advice than to publish one that cannot be checked.
    """
    return tuple(item for item in items if resolve(source, item.field_path) is not None)


def order(items: tuple[Advice, ...]) -> tuple[Advice, ...]:
    """Sort by severity, then by code, so two runs of one input agree.

    The secondary key is not decoration: rules fire in whatever order
    their module happens to evaluate them, and a list that reshuffles
    between identical runs is one a reader cannot diff.
    """
    return tuple(sorted(items, key=lambda a: (_SEVERITY_RANK.get(a.severity, 9), a.code)))

Advice is text a reader acts on, so the tests that matter are about what
it is not allowed to be: unverifiable (a citation that resolves nowhere),
or unstable (two runs of one input disagreeing about the order). Both
failures look like working software until somebody trusts the output.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

import pytest
from pydantic import ValidationError

from planbench_decision.advice import Advice, keep_resolvable, order


def advice(**overrides: Any) -> Advice:
    base: dict[str, Any] = {
        "code": "P1",
        "kind": "preflight",
        "severity": "material",
        "claim": "the two candidates see different worlds",
        "ground": "one reads a static map, the other only LiDAR",
        "field_path": "candidates[0].observation_class",
        "do": "run them on the same observation class",
        "do_not": "read the ranking as a planner comparison",
    }
    base.update(overrides)
    return Advice(**base)


REPORT: dict[str, Any] = {
    "candidates": [{"observation_class": "map_static"}, {"observation_class": "lidar_only"}],
    "decision_card": {"status": "NEAR_EQUIVALENT"},
}


class TestEveryPieceOfAdviceCitesSomethingReal:
    def test_a_resolvable_citation_survives(self) -> None:
        assert keep_resolvable((advice(),), REPORT) == (advice(),)

    def test_a_citation_that_resolves_nowhere_is_dropped(self) -> None:
        """The reader cannot tell an unverifiable rule from a
        hallucinating model, so neither is published."""
        assert keep_resolvable((advice(field_path="candidates[0].no_such_field"),), REPORT) == ()

    def test_an_index_past_the_end_is_dropped(self) -> None:
        assert keep_resolvable((advice(field_path="candidates[7].observation_class"),), REPORT) == ()

    def test_the_rule_applies_to_rules_too_not_only_to_the_model(self) -> None:
        """A rule pointing at a field this particular report does not
        carry makes exactly the claim a fabrication would."""
        kept = keep_resolvable(
            (advice(code="R1"), advice(code="R2", field_path="absent.path")), REPORT
        )
        assert [a.code for a in kept] == ["R1"]


class TestOrderIsStable:
    def test_blocking_comes_before_material_before_disclosure(self) -> None:
        items = (
            advice(code="A", severity="disclosure"),
            advice(code="B", severity="blocking"),
            advice(code="C", severity="material"),
        )
        assert [a.code for a in order(items)] == ["B", "C", "A"]

    def test_two_orderings_of_one_input_agree(self) -> None:
        """Rules fire in whatever order their module evaluates them; a
        list that reshuffles between identical runs cannot be diffed."""
        items = tuple(advice(code=c) for c in ("Z", "A", "M"))
        assert order(items) == order(tuple(reversed(items)))

    def test_ties_break_on_code_rather_than_on_arrival(self) -> None:
        items = (advice(code="P9"), advice(code="P2"))
        assert [a.code for a in order(items)] == ["P2", "P9"]

    def test_an_unknown_severity_sorts_last_rather_than_crashing(self) -> None:
        """Advice arriving from a model layer is validated, but a future
        severity added upstream must not take the ordering down."""
        loose = advice()
        widened = Advice.model_construct(**{**loose.model_dump(), "severity": "someday"})
        assert order((widened, advice(code="A", severity="blocking")))[0].code == "A"


class TestTheShapeRefusesWhatWouldMislead:
    def test_advice_is_frozen(self) -> None:
        """A caller that could edit `do_not` could erase the forbidden
        move from a copy the reader sees."""
        with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
            advice().code = "changed"

    def test_a_forbidden_move_may_be_empty_but_must_be_deliberate(self) -> None:
        """Empty is allowed — some situations have no tempting wrong
        move — and it defaults to empty rather than to a placeholder,
        so a rule that never set it reads as "none" rather than as
        advice nobody wrote."""
        assert advice(do_not="").do_not == ""

    @pytest.mark.parametrize("field", ["code", "kind", "severity", "claim", "ground", "do"])
    def test_the_fields_a_reader_needs_are_required(self, field: str) -> None:
        payload = advice().model_dump()
        payload.pop(field)
        with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
            Advice(**payload)

    def test_a_kind_outside_the_lifecycle_is_refused(self) -> None:
        with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
            advice(kind="whenever")

    def test_a_severity_outside_the_three_is_refused(self) -> None:
        with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
            advice(severity="catastrophic")

tool_input.feature: Results-prose drafter for a stored Decision Card — a deterministic "results brief" of numbered, field-cited sentences, optionally phrased by a model that may not introduce a number. NOT redundant with GET /decisions/{run_id}/report.md, but overlapping: report.md already renders provenance, sample, the gate table, scope, sensitivity margins and the human record. What report.md does NOT contain is every statistical number on the card — `_card()` in apps/api/planbench_api/decision_markdown.py prints `recommended.stack`, `recommended.candidate_id`, `alternative` (broken, see risks), `status`, `contracts_version`, the scope blockquote, then jumps straight to `_sensitivity()`. It never prints delta_u_vs_second, delta_u_mean, ci95, n_episodes, effect_size, decision_utility, the four objectives, or pareto_label. It also never prints G2's contractually-mandated collision sentence or G4's host-only caveat, which live in the gate dicts it renders around. A student handed report.md today has the verdict word and no number to quote it with. Build recommendation: do NOT ship a second competing document. Build one deterministic module that produces an ordered, cited brief, render it as a new "## Results" section inside the existing render_decision_markdown(), and expose the brief as JSON for the UI and the model layer.

data_sources.notes: delta_u_vs_second is the MEDIAN paired difference; delta_u_mean is the MEAN, and ci95 is the interval of the mean, not of the median (docstring lines 148-157 records a real run where median +0.0131 sat outside a CI of [+0.0028, +0.0111]). effect_size is float|None — None means every episode gave the identical difference, not zero effect. weight_stability_margin / anchor_stability are None unless the phase-5 sweeps ran. robustness_margin is declared here and is NEVER set by build_decision_card, so it is null on every card the pipeline produces today (verified: no producer outside neighborhood.py's docstring).

This exact dict is what becomes report['decision_card'] and StoredDecisionRun.card (selection.py:789, decision_service.py:_store). CRITICAL: `tie_break_reason` is a field on the DecisionCard model but is deliberately EXCLUDED from to_json_dict (see the field comment at card.py:279-283). It therefore does not exist in any stored report or card. Every field_path of the form decision_card.tie_break_reason is unresolvable in production. to_json_dict also runs assert_no_banned_language over the payload on the way out.

AlternativeBlock has NO `stack` field — only candidate_id and reason. build_decision_card sets alternative only from the Pareto frontier via _alternative_block(); it is None when no Pareto analysis ran, when the frontier held only the winner, or when no frontier member was scored. recommendation.runner_up_id is explicitly NOT the alternative (module docstring lines 17-22).

Reaches the report as report['manifest'] (selection.py:797) and StoredDecisionRun.manifest. bootstrap is {'seed': int, 'n_resamples': int} — the two values that make ci95 rebuildable. WARNING: constraints is TaskConstraints.model_dump(), and n_min_evaluation_episodes is a @property on TaskConstraints (task_profile.py:316), not a field — so `manifest.constraints.n_min_evaluation_episodes` does NOT resolve. Use `sample.n_min_required` instead. Confirmed resolvable constraint fields: success_rate_min, collision_probability_max, no_path_rate_max, goal_tolerance_m, goal_tolerance_rad, episode_timeout_s, stuck_threshold_s, clearance_warning_m.

The bootstrap resamples EPISODE CONTEXTS (not metrics) at 1000 resamples, percentile [2.5, 97.5] over bootstrap MEANS — so ci95 is a percentile CI of the mean paired difference. status is CLEAR_RECOMMENDATION iff ci95 excludes zero, else NEAR_EQUIVALENT. delta_iqr and runner_up_id and ranking exist on Recommendation/PairedComparison but are NOT carried onto the card, so they are unavailable to a prose layer reading the stored report. No p-value is computed anywhere (HĐ-11.3 forbids one without an effect size). TIE_BREAK_ORDER is the four declared rungs, in Vietnamese, in order.

data_sources.symbol: GateReport.to_card / G2Result / G4Result / G5Result / G4_HOST_ONLY_CAVEAT / assert_no_banned_language / BANNED_PHRASES
data_sources.notes: G1/G3/G6 render as bare 'pass'/'fail' strings; G2/G4/G5 as dicts. G2.statement is the contract-mandated sentence naming distinct-run count, the 3/N bound and the phrase 'dưới phân phối kịch bản đã mô phỏng' — it is what stops '0 collisions' being read as 'no collisions happen'. G2.upper_bound_95 is None once any collision was observed. G4.status is the Literal 'screened_on_host' and is the ONLY value this project can produce (no target board), so G4.caveat applies to every run. G5.status is 'estimated_from_structure' or 'declared_by_author'; 'verified_on_target' does not exist. assert_no_banned_language(payload, where=...) walks strings/dicts/lists and raises BannedLanguageError on 'an toàn' (regex an\s+toàn, case-insensitive) or \bTCO\b — reuse it, do not re-implement it.

This is the authoritative shape of the dict every field_path is resolved against. decision_card and manifest are present-and-null on unranked runs; why_no_card is present ONLY on the unranked branch (line 730) and on the interrupted-before-any-episode report (line 852). gate_only_deployment distinguishes 'nobody survived the gates' from 'this deployment can never rank (HĐ-8.4)'. candidates[i].gates is GateReport.to_card() so the full gate paths are candidates[i].gates.G2.statement etc. The card's own copy is a LIST: decision_card.gates[i].G2.statement, sorted by candidate_id.

resolve(report, 'a.b[0].c') walks dots and [i], returns None when absent. critique() filters its own findings through it (line 515) — the rules hold themselves to the same bar they hold the model to. Severity vocabulary to reuse verbatim: blocking = the stated conclusion does not stand on this evidence; material = it stands only with a condition attached; disclosure = it stands and must still be said out loud. Note _rule_tie_break reads decision_card.tie_break_reason, which never resolves in a production report (see card.py notes) — the rule is silently dead outside test fixtures that hand-build the dict.

data_sources.symbol: critique_with_model / CritiqueResult / ScoredFinding / _summarise / critique_schema / MAX_MODEL_FINDINGS / CRITIQUE_MAX_TOKENS
data_sources.notes: The exact precedent to copy. Deterministic half is computed first and survives every failure path (provider raises, returns no structured output, fails validation, uses banned language). Model output is validated by a frozen extra='forbid' Pydantic _Payload, then each finding's field_path is run through resolve(); non-resolving ones are dropped and counted in `fabricated`. assert_no_banned_language is applied to the model's prose and, if it trips, the prose is discarded while the deterministic findings are still returned with `refused` set. Never raises. _summarise() shows the model a trimmed report (no per-episode tables) because a longer prompt degrades structured output.

THE REDUNDANCY CHECK. This is everything the existing export says about the card. Confirmed absent: delta_u_vs_second, delta_u_mean, ci95, n_episodes, effect_size, decision_utility, objectives, pareto_label, decision_mode_label, declared_assumptions, manifest_ref, approval, bootstrap seed/n_resamples, G2.statement, G2.upper_bound_95, G4.caveat, G4.p99_ms vs threshold_ms, G5.status. NOT_MEASURED = 'not measured' is the established rendering of null and must be reused, not redefined. _text() escapes pipes and newlines for table safety.

GET /decisions/{run_id}/report.md returns PlainTextResponse with Content-Disposition attachment. GET /decisions/{run_id}/critique takes ?use_model=false and branches: rules-only, or critique_with_model(stored.report, agent.provider) via get_agent_service(request, user). Counts are always derived from the findings inside _critique_resource, never passed in. Copy this shape exactly.

run.card is literally report['decision_card'] and run.manifest is report['manifest'] (decision_service.py:_store, lines 674-687). So a prose layer can take the report dict alone and reach everything; it does not need a second argument. ranked is a property == (card is not None).

objectives on the card is exactly {'U_R','U_S','U_E','U_C'} floats for the WINNER only — no rival's objectives are on the card, so the prose cannot compare objective-by-objective from the card alone (they are in report['candidates'][i] only as success_rate / pooled_p99_latency_ms, not as utilities). decision_mode_label is DecisionSettings.card_label and is what names the weighting the reader is being shown.

Three values only. build_decision_card writes UNCERTAIN_DOMINANCE when no Pareto analysis ran at all (card.py:505-509), so on a phase-3 run the label means 'not analysed' and NOT 'analysed and inconclusive' — and certainly not 'not dominated'. LIKELY_DOMINATED can never appear on a recommended candidate (_require_not_dominated raises).

rules.claim: the recommended stack is better than the runner-up
rules.condition: decision_card.status == "NEAR_EQUIVALENT"
rules.suggested_action: Emit the tie sentence instead: "The paired 95% interval for ΔU is [lo, hi] over n episodes and contains zero, so the two candidates are statistically indistinguishable on decision_utility. <stack> was selected by the declared secondary criteria of HĐ-11.3, not by a measured margin." Cite decision_card.evidence.ci95 and decision_card.status.
rules.forbidden_action: Any comparative or superiority verb applied to the recommendation against the runner-up — better, outperforms, beats, wins, superior, improves on, faster, more efficient — and any phrasing that presents delta_u_vs_second as a demonstrated advantage. NEAR_EQUIVALENT means the interval admits no difference; the winner is a tie-break outcome.

rules.claim: candidate X won on <named tie-break criterion>
rules.condition: decision_card.status == "NEAR_EQUIVALENT" and "tie_break_reason" not in decision_card (which is always, because DecisionCard.to_json_dict deliberately omits it)
rules.suggested_action: Say only that a tie-break decided it and that the ladder is the four declared criteria of HĐ-11.3 in fixed order (TIE_BREAK_ORDER in stats.py), without asserting which rung fired. Better: fix the pipeline first — see open_questions.
rules.forbidden_action: Naming a specific rung ("won on lower U_C", "won on fewer tunable parameters", "won for being modular"). The string that says which rung fired exists on the Recommendation and the DecisionCard model but is stripped by to_json_dict, so it is not in the stored report. Inferring it from the objectives block is a guess with the card's authority.

rules.condition: always, whenever the prose mentions decision_card.evidence.delta_u_vs_second or delta_u_mean
rules.suggested_action: Every mention of a ΔU figure must carry decision_card.evidence.ci95 and decision_card.evidence.n_episodes in the same sentence, and must name it as a paired difference against the runner-up over the shared episode set.
rules.forbidden_action: Printing a ΔU number without its interval and its n. A point estimate alone reads as a measured fact rather than the centre of an interval, and the whole reason this platform computes a paired bootstrap is that the point estimate is not the finding.

rules.claim: median ΔU = a (95% CI [lo, hi])
rules.condition: the prose places decision_card.evidence.ci95 beside decision_card.evidence.delta_u_vs_second
rules.suggested_action: Name both statistics explicitly: "median paired ΔU = <delta_u_vs_second>, mean paired ΔU = <delta_u_mean>, 95% bootstrap CI of the mean [<lo>, <hi>]". The card's own docstring records a run where the median sat outside the CI (+0.0131 against [+0.0028, +0.0111]) precisely because they are two different statistics.
rules.forbidden_action: Presenting ci95 as the confidence interval of delta_u_vs_second, or writing "ΔU = x ± y" in a way that binds the interval to the median. paired_bootstrap_ci resamples and takes percentiles of bootstrap MEANS; the interval is the mean's.

rules.claim: the effect size was 0 / there was no effect
rules.condition: decision_card.evidence.effect_size is null
rules.suggested_action: Render as "paired effect size (Cohen's d_z): not defined — every episode produced the same difference, so the standardised effect divides by a spread of zero" (stats.py _paired_effect_size). Use the established NOT_MEASURED wording where a short cell is needed.
rules.forbidden_action: Rendering null as 0, as "—", as a blank, or as "no effect". Null here means the sample says nothing about variability, which is the opposite of saying the effect is nil, and it commonly happens with deterministic planners on a static map.

rules.claim: the recommendation is stable / robust
rules.condition: any of decision_card.evidence.weight_stability_margin, decision_card.evidence.anchor_stability, decision_card.evidence.robustness_margin is null — robustness_margin is null on every card the current pipeline produces, since build_decision_card never sets it
rules.suggested_action: Name each of the three sweeps and say which did not run, using the existing 'not measured' wording. If all three are null, state it in one sentence: "None of the three sensitivity margins were measured. That is not the same as their being wide."
rules.forbidden_action: Silence about an unmeasured margin, a blank, or any word implying it was checked — stable, robust, insensitive, holds under reweighting. HĐ-12 defines null as "not measured", and a plausible default would read as "measured and fine".

rules.claim: the recommended stack had no collisions
rules.condition: the prose mentions collisions, and candidates[i].gates.G2.observed == 0
rules.suggested_action: Quote candidates[i].gates.G2.statement verbatim. It already names the distinct-run count, the 3/N upper bound and the conditioning phrase "dưới phân phối kịch bản đã mô phỏng". Quote candidates[i].gates.G2.n_distinct_episodes as the denominator, never n_runs, and carry G2.note when present.
rules.forbidden_action: "No collisions", "collision-free", "zero collision rate", or any unconditional collision claim; and computing or quoting a bound over n_runs rather than n_distinct_episodes. Zero events in N trials bounds p by ~3/N at 95% only under the distribution simulated; dropping the condition is the exact overclaim the gate's mandated sentence exists to prevent.

rules.claim: the stack meets its control-period budget
rules.condition: candidates[i].gates.G4.status == "screened_on_host" — the only value this project can produce
rules.suggested_action: Quote p99_ms against threshold_ms and attach candidates[i].gates.G4.caveat (G4_HOST_ONLY_CAVEAT) to the same sentence. Phrase it as a screening result: failing on the host proves failure on target; passing proves nothing.
rules.forbidden_action: Stating or implying real-time behaviour on a robot or target board, using "verified", "meets real-time requirements", or converting host milliseconds to a target-board figure. No conversion factor exists and none may be invented (§17 ban 8) — A* is memory-bound, DWA is compute-bound, and they do not scale together.

rules.claim: the p99 latency figures describe the stacks
rules.condition: measurement_environment.warning is not null
rules.suggested_action: Attach the warning text to every sentence citing candidates[i].pooled_p99_latency_ms or gates.G4.p99_ms, and say the number measures this machine as much as the candidate.
rules.forbidden_action: Quoting a latency figure as a property of the candidate. The card's own BenchmarkHost docstring records the same rrtstar+dwa at 59.30 ms unpinned and 16.10 ms pinned — a factor of 3.7, larger than the gap between candidates, and it has already been misread once as a property of a stack.

rules.claim: the stack fits the memory budget
rules.condition: candidates[i].gates.G5.status == "declared_by_author"
rules.suggested_action: Say the memory figure was declared by the candidate's author at registration and never measured, quoting candidates[i].gates.G5.note. Never substitute peak_rss_mb_diagnostic for it.
rules.forbidden_action: Presenting memory_estimate_mb as a measurement, or quoting peak_rss_mb_diagnostic as the gate's number — it is the RSS of a Python process and is wrong against a C++ board budget by an unpredictable order of magnitude (§17 ban 13).

rules.claim: this stack is the right choice
rules.condition: always, on any run that produced a card
rules.suggested_action: Bind the conclusion to identity.task_profile_id and decision_card.recommendation_scope (MISSION_LEVEL / DEPLOYMENT_LEVEL / ROBUST_DEPLOYMENT_LEVEL) in the opening or closing sentence, and name decision_card.decision_mode_label so the reader knows which weighting produced decision_utility.
rules.forbidden_action: Any generalisation past the named deployment — "for warehouse AMRs", "in general", "for this class of environment", "we recommend A* over RRT*". Carrying the recommendation to another deployment is a claim the run did not make (HĐ-1.4), and a document travels further than the screen it came from.

rules.claim: you could also ship the second-ranked candidate
rules.condition: decision_card.alternative is null
rules.suggested_action: State that no alternative was established, and why it could be any of three things: no Pareto analysis ran, the frontier held only the recommendation, or no frontier member was scored into the ranking. When decision_card.alternative is non-null, quote alternative.candidate_id and alternative.reason.
rules.forbidden_action: Naming the statistical runner-up as "the alternative" or "a viable second choice". The runner-up is second on one weighted sum and can be worse on every objective at once; the card's alternative is a different claim sourced only from the Pareto frontier, and card.py keeps the two deliberately unwired. Also: alternative has no `stack` field, only candidate_id and reason.

rules.claim: the recommendation is not dominated by any rival
rules.condition: decision_card.pareto_label == "UNCERTAIN_DOMINANCE"
rules.suggested_action: Say the dominance analysis did not run or was underpowered, so no statement about domination is available for this run. On PARETO_FRONTIER, the positive claim is allowed and must cite the label.
rules.forbidden_action: "Not dominated", "on the Pareto frontier", "best on all objectives", or omitting the label entirely. build_decision_card writes UNCERTAIN_DOMINANCE when no Pareto analysis ran at all, so on most runs the label means "not analysed" — HĐ-10.1's own name for "not enough data to conclude".

rules.claim: the run supports the deployment's declared collision risk
rules.condition: sample.n_episodes < sample.n_min_required
rules.suggested_action: Open the brief with the shortfall, quoting both numbers, and state that the collision claim is not supported at this sample size. Note that sample.n_min_required is the resolvable path — manifest.constraints.n_min_evaluation_episodes does not resolve, because it is a @property and not dumped.
rules.forbidden_action: Quoting the G2 bound or any risk statement at all, and treating a short run as a valid smaller experiment. The episode count is a consequence of the declared collision risk (ceil(3/p_max)), not a taste setting.

rules.claim: every candidate faced the same evaluation
rules.condition: sample.interrupted is true, or early_stop.stopped is non-empty, or two candidates[i].n_episodes differ
rules.suggested_action: Name each retired candidate with its episodes_run against episodes_planned and the rule that retired it, and say a retired candidate's numbers rest on fewer episodes. For an interrupted sweep, quote sample.n_episodes beside sample.n_episodes_requested.
rules.forbidden_action: Quoting a retired or short-sampled candidate's success rate or latency beside a survivor's as if the denominators matched, or describing an interrupted run as a deliberately-sized one.

rules.claim: candidate X came second / was close behind
rules.condition: candidates[i].cleared_gates is false
rules.suggested_action: Quote a blocked candidate only as eliminated, naming which gates blocked it and after how many runs. Its success rate may be reported as a measurement, never as a ranking position.
rules.forbidden_action: Placing a gate-failing candidate anywhere in an ordering, or describing its score as competitive. Gates run before scoring; a candidate that fails one is not a worse choice, it is not a choice.

rules.forbidden_action: Naming any candidate as recommended, best, or leading; computing a ΔU from the report's per-candidate numbers; or presenting a gate-only run as an inconclusive comparison rather than as the result it is.

rules.claim: the difference is statistically established

rules.forbidden_action: Calling a result "statistically significant" or quoting a p-value. risks: REDUNDANCY, stated honestly: about 40% of a naive Feature 5 already exists. report.md already renders provenance (run id, deployment, experiment scope, contracts version, git sha, anchor config, created_at), the sample block with its n_min, the full gate table with the mixed-observation and early-stop warnings, the scope blockquote, the three sensitivity margins with 'not measured' spelled out, and the human review/approval record. Re-rendering any of that in a second document creates two artefacts that can disagree about the same run. The genuinely missing half is the evidence numbers and the gate caveats, and that is what should be built.

BUG FOUND, unrelated to whether Feature 5 ships: decision_markdown.py line 203 reads `alternative.get('stack')`, but AlternativeBlock has only `candidate_id` and `reason` — there is no `stack` field. Every exported report.md therefore prints 'Alternative | not measured' even when the card names one, and 'not measured' is exactly the wording reserved for 'this was never computed'. The export is currently asserting the strongest possible non-claim about a field that is populated.

BUG FOUND, load-bearing for this feature: DecisionCard.tie_break_reason is deliberately excluded from to_json_dict (card.py:279-283, 'kept off to_json_dict for that reason'), and selection.py sets report['decision_card'] = card.to_json_dict() while decision_service._store sets StoredDecisionRun.card = report['decision_card']. So the string that says WHICH tie-break rung decided a NEAR_EQUIVALENT run exists nowhere in any stored artefact. Two consequences: (a) self_check._rule_tie_break's field_path decision_card.tie_break_reason never resolves in production, so WON_ON_TIE_BREAK is silently dead outside test fixtures that hand-build the dict (tests/test_self_check.py:141 sets it manually); (b) the NEAR_EQUIVALENT prose cannot name the rung without inventing it. The card's comment says the field is 'available to the UI', but nothing in apps/web reads it.

PRECISION DRIFT between the brief and any other rendering. decision_markdown._number formats with %.3g; the web UI formats ΔU with toFixed(6). If the prose layer picks a third precision, the same run yields three different-looking numbers and a reader cannot tell whether they are the same measurement. Fix the rendering in one place — Citation.rendered — and have report.md and the UI read that string rather than reformat the float.

MODEL-LAYER NUMBER LAUNDERING. critique.py's fabrication check is a field_path resolution test, which does not transfer: prose contains numerals, not paths. A model asked to 'write this more fluently' will round 0.0131 to 0.013, convert 12.5 ms to 0.0125 s, or turn a 0.9 success rate into 90%, and each of those is a new number the deterministic layer never authorised. The numeric-token check against Citation.rendered is the substitute and must be written before the model layer is enabled, not after.

A FLUENT PARAGRAPH IS MORE PERSUASIVE THAN A TABLE. This is the reason the feature is risky at all: the same caveats that a reader skims past in a Markdown table become invisible when smoothed into prose, and prose is what gets pasted into a report and defended in a viva. The mitigation is structural — caveat sentences are emitted by the deterministic layer as first-class Sentence objects with their own rule_codes and citations, they sit in the same ordered list as the result sentences, and the model may reorder within a section but may not drop a sentence. This is exactly the 'may reorder and extend but never overrule' contract critique.py already holds.

OBJECTIVE-BY-OBJECTIVE PROSE IS NOT AVAILABLE FROM THE CARD. decision_card.objectives holds U_R/U_S/U_E/U_C for the WINNER only. No rival's utilities are on the card or in the report — report['candidates'][i] carries success_rate, pooled_p99_latency_ms, replan_count and the gate dicts, but no objective values. Any sentence of the form 'X was better on safety but worse on efficiency' cannot be grounded and must not be attempted from a stored run.

GATE PATHS DIFFER BETWEEN THE TWO COPIES. report['candidates'][i]['gates'] is a dict keyed G1..G6, while report['decision_card']['gates'] is a LIST of the same dicts sorted by candidate_id. Citations must use candidates[i].gates.G2.statement, not decision_card.gates.G2.statement, or resolve() returns None and the sentence is dropped as fabricated by its own layer.

DETERMINISM UNDER THE PROJECT'S OWN RULE. The brief must be a pure function of the report dict — no clock, no git shell-out, no locale-dependent number formatting, no dict-iteration-order dependence. card.py already pays this price deliberately (Provenance is passed in rather than discovered, gates are sorted by id so a rebuild is byte-identical). A prose layer that sorts candidates by ranking rather than by id, or formats with the ambient locale, breaks the same rebuild guarantee.

LANGUAGE MIXING. G2.statement, G2.note, G5.note, G4.caveat, AlternativeBlock.reason and every TIE_BREAK_ORDER rung are Vietnamese; the existing report.md prose and the critique findings are English. A brief that quotes the mandated sentences verbatim (which it must — paraphrasing G2.statement is how the bound's conditioning gets lost) will be bilingual. Decide this deliberately rather than letting a model 'helpfully' translate, since a translated G2 statement is no longer the contract artefact.
open_questions: Should tie_break_reason be added to DecisionCard.to_json_dict before this feature is built? It is the only honest source for the NEAR_EQUIVALENT sentence, it is already a field on the model, and adding it would simultaneously revive self_check's WON_ON_TIE_BREAK rule, which is currently dead in production. The card docstring gives a reason for the exclusion ('outside HĐ-12's field list'), so this is a contract question and needs approval, not a patch. If the answer is no, the prose rule above stands and the sentence stays deliberately vague.

Is the audience a student's report or a reviewer's sign-off? The task says 'a paragraph a student could put in a report', but the module would sit beside critique.py, whose stated audience is 'a human who is about to sign off'. These want different defaults: a student paragraph wants the numbers inline and the caveats as clauses; a sign-off brief wants the caveats as separate, countable, un-droppable sentences. The Sentence/section model above serves both, but only one can be the default rendering in report.md.

Should the brief be gated on review or approval? report.md deliberately is not ('it is a description of what was measured, and reading it is the act that approval follows'), while approved_config.yaml is. A fluent paragraph asserting a recommendation is closer to the second in how it will be used, and drafting one for an unreviewed run may be handing out a conclusion before anyone has read the objections.

Should the deterministic brief refuse outright when self_check.critique() returns a blocking finding? There is a coherent design where a run carrying DELTA_U_CI_STRADDLES_ZERO or SAMPLE_BELOW_N_MIN gets no result paragraph at all, only the eliminations — on the same logic that build_decision_card refuses rather than warns for a dominated recommendation. The alternative is to draft the paragraph with the blocking finding as its first sentence. The first is safer and more annoying; this is a product call.

Does the brief include the critique findings, or stay independent of them? Both read the same report and both are derived-not-stored, so they could be one endpoint. Keeping them apart means a reader can get a fluent paragraph without ever seeing the objections, which is the failure mode this whole layer exists to prevent.

What does the brief do with report['checks'] (the check_* results appended by run_comparison)? I did not read the check objects' shape and cannot say what fields they expose or whether a failed check is representable in the report dict at all — do not cite anything under `checks` until that is verified.

Confirm empirically against a real stored run before writing any citation. Consequence a diagnosis must respect: an episode with both a no_path event and a collision is bucketed 'collision', so the no_path histogram and G1's own numerator agree exactly (both read failure_reason == 'no_path') but both under-count no_path when a collision co-occurs. Only 8 of these 23 fields survive into the report's episodes rows.

The threshold side of every gate. n_min_evaluation_episodes is a property = ceil(round(3/collision_probability_max, 6)); t_cycle_ms is a property = control_period*1000. no_path_rate_max defaults to 0.02. goal_tolerance_rad is validated to be >= pi (heading unconstrained) so 'tighten heading' is not an available knob. These values reach a stored report ONLY through manifest.constraints - and the manifest is null in every card-less run.

manifest.constraints is the ONLY place a stored report carries success_rate_min / no_path_rate_max / episode_timeout_s / goal_tolerance_m, and manifest.episode_contexts.evaluation is the ONLY place episode_context_id can be joined back to a mission_id and seed. Verified on disk: every one of the 11 stored reports with decision_card == null also has manifest == null. That is exactly the run a gate-failure explainer is for, so the explainer must not depend on either.
