The precedent for any LLM layer over this feature: rules run first and survive every failure path, the model may reorder and add at most 3, every model citation is checked with the same resolve() and dropped+counted as 'fabricated' if it does not resolve, and banned language voids the prose but never the rules. _summarise deliberately strips per-episode tables from the model's view - which is precisely the evidence this feature needs, so an advice-with-model variant needs its own summariser, not this one.

The route shape to copy: read-only, derived, nothing stored, so a rule added tomorrow applies to every run already on disk. Counts are derived from the findings inside _critique_resource, never passed in. _without_episode_tables strips candidates[i].episodes from LIST responses only; the single-run GET keeps them, so the advice endpoint reading stored.report directly does see the episode table.

_store writes report=<the dict run_comparison returned> verbatim, so the stored report and the on-disk comparison_report.json are the same shape. trace(run_id, candidate_id, episode_context_id) is the endpoint an episode-level diagnosis should point the reader at; it validates the episode against sample.episode_context_ids. TaskProfileService.load(profile_id) can recover the live thresholds for a card-less run - but doing so silently breaks the 'field_path resolves against the source' invariant unless the profile is merged into the source dict the paths are resolved against.

rules.claim: This candidate was eliminated at G1: it returned no route on more of the evaluation set than the deployment permits.
rules.condition: candidates[i].gates.G1 == 'fail'. Evidence pass: when candidates[i].episodes resolves, count rows with failure_reason == 'no_path' and collect their episode_context_id; that count over candidates[i].n_episodes reproduces G1's own rate exactly, because _gate_1 reads the same field. When episodes does not resolve (older reports), fall back to field_path 'candidates[i].gates.G1' and a ground that states the verdict only. The threshold itself (constraints.no_path_rate_max, default 0.02) is NOT in the report; quote it only when manifest.constraints.no_path_rate_max resolves.
rules.suggested_action: Open the no_path episodes by episode_context_id via GET /api/v1/decisions/{run_id}/traces/{candidate_id}/{episode_context_id} and check whether the goal is reachable at all. If every candidate fails no_path on the same episode_context_ids, the suspect is the deployment rather than the stack - MetricError already refuses a mission with no route on the map, and validate_missions_on_map refuses the five ways a profile and a map disagree. If only this candidate does, register one with a different global planner or a costmap inflation that leaves the corridor passable.
rules.forbidden_action: Do not raise constraints.no_path_rate_max so the observed rate fits, and do not swap the mission or the map until this candidate finds routes. HD-8.4: a threshold is a declaration, not a knob - lowering one to obtain a Decision Card is exactly the HD-15.3 failure. HD-15.1 criterion 7 records changing the mission and changing the traffic among four result-driven edits that passed the entire acceptance round undetected. A threshold may move only because the old number was concluded wrong, and the reason must be written where a later reader finds it.

rules.claim: This candidate was eliminated at G2 with collisions on the record, so no collision-probability bound may be quoted for it at all.
rules.condition: candidates[i].gates.G2.result == 'fail' AND candidates[i].gates.G2.observed > 0. Evidence pass: from candidates[i].episodes, list episode_context_id where collision_count > 0, and read min_clearance on the surviving rows to say how close the rest came. Never cite gates.G2.upper_bound_95 here: it is null by design once a collision is observed, and resolve() treats null as absent, so the advice would be silently dropped.
rules.suggested_action: Open every episode whose collision_count > 0 and read its trace; min_clearance on the non-colliding rows tells you whether the rest were comfortable or merely lucky. Register a candidate that clears these specific episodes. The eliminated candidate may still be reported - HD-10.1 keeps everyone in the gate table - but only as eliminated, never as a runner-up.
rules.forbidden_action: Do not raise constraints.collision_probability_max, and do not quote a rule-of-three upper bound anyway: gates.G2.upper_bound_95 is null on purpose because the rule of three applies to zero-event data only (HD-7.1), and computing one regardless is arithmetic dressed as evidence. S17 ban 10 forbids the word 'an toan' beside any number this system produced; S17 ban 11 forbids declaring deterministic obstacles with seed_time_offset = 0 and then counting N runs as N independent samples.

rules.claim: This candidate saw zero collisions but on fewer distinct episodes than the declared risk requires, so the run cannot support a collision claim for it.
rules.condition: candidates[i].gates.G2.result == 'fail' AND candidates[i].gates.G2.observed == 0 AND candidates[i].gates.G2.n_distinct_episodes < candidates[i].gates.G2.n_min. Report gates.G2.n_min (present) rather than recomputing ceil(3/collision_probability_max), since collision_probability_max is not in the report. Suppress the shortfall arithmetic when self_check has already emitted SAMPLE_BELOW_N_MIN for the same run and sample.n_episodes == gates.G2.n_runs; suppress the replay half entirely when n_distinct_episodes < n_runs, which G2_REPLAYED_EPISODES already owns.
rules.suggested_action: Run (n_min - n_distinct_episodes) more episodes with seeds that actually produce different episodes. HD-7.1 explicitly permits running short without touching the deployment: pass the episode count at the CLI and let G2 report fail carrying the sentence it already writes - the measurement is identical either way, and the difference is that the system declares itself short rather than lowering the bar to meet itself.
rules.forbidden_action: Do not raise constraints.collision_probability_max to shrink N_min to fit the machine hours available. HD-7.1: the arrow runs one way - declared risk implies N_min implies hours - and reading it backwards lowers the customer's safety standard to fit your schedule. This has already happened once: the reference warehouse declared 3% with the reason written into the profile as 'vi run phai chia se may'. A busy machine is not a property of the warehouse.

rules.claim: This candidate was eliminated at G3: it reached the goal on fewer episodes than the deployment requires.
rules.condition: candidates[i].gates.G3 == 'fail'. Evidence pass: histogram failure_reason over candidates[i].episodes into the four FailureReason buckets, name the dominant one, and carry replan_count from the same rows. Cite candidates[i].success_rate (always present, and 0.0 still resolves) as the observed value; the threshold constraints.success_rate_min is NOT in the report, so quote it only when manifest.constraints.success_rate_min resolves. When episodes does not resolve, fall back to field_path 'candidates[i].success_rate' with a ground carrying the rate alone.
rules.suggested_action: Read the failure_reason histogram, because each of the four buckets lands on a different layer: no_path is the global planner (and G1 already scored it separately for exactly this reason); collision also fails G2 and should be read there; timeout and stuck are the local controller or the replanning budget, and replan_count on the same row separates 'recovered on the first try' from 'replanned forty times and timed out'. Register a candidate that addresses the dominant bucket. If the histogram is flat across every candidate, suspect the deployment and check it with the test bench on one episode before spending another sweep.
rules.forbidden_action: Do not lower constraints.success_rate_min to below the observed rate, do not raise constraints.episode_timeout_s to convert timeouts into successes, and do not widen constraints.goal_tolerance_m to convert near-arrivals into arrivals. All three are HD-8.4's threshold-as-knob and fail HD-15.3's question - is this number from the site, or from what my machine and my code can manage? goal_tolerance_rad is already on the record as one of the four result-driven edits found on 2026-08-11, and TaskConstraints now refuses any value below pi outright.

rules.claim: This candidate failed G4 on a host that was not pinned, so the failure may belong to the machine rather than to the candidate.
rules.condition: candidates[i].gates.G4.result == 'fail' AND measurement_environment.warning is truthy. (Equivalent structural test when the warning string is absent: benchmark_host.cpu_affinity and benchmark_host.logical_cores both resolve and len(cpu_affinity) == logical_cores, which BenchmarkHost.is_pinned reports as not pinned.) Emit this INSTEAD of G4_BUDGET_EXCEEDED, never both.
rules.suggested_action: Re-run pinned before reading this as a property of the candidate. HD-7.4 records the same rrtstar+dwa measured at 59.30 ms pooled p99 unpinned and 16.10 ms pinned to two cores - a factor of 3.7, larger than the gap between the candidates - and contract 3.0.0 records A* being eliminated at G4 for the machine's load rather than its own cost. Also confirm no second evaluation run shared the machine: HD-7.4 forbids two at once, because the core-selection rule is deterministic and both runs pin to the identical mask.
rules.forbidden_action: Do not raise robot.control_period so the budget accommodates the measurement. HD-7.2 records both reference profiles declaring control_period 0.1 (10 Hz) instead of 20 Hz with the reason written in the file as 'DWA Python khong tinh noi mot buoc dieu khien trong 50 ms' - the gate threshold was doubled because the candidate could not clear it - and loosening it buys nothing anyway, since simulation_dt = min(0.05, control_period) makes 10 Hz and 20 Hz integrate the identical world. Do not multiply p99_ms by any host-to-board conversion factor (S17 ban 8, HD-7.2: A* is memory-bound and DWA compute-bound, so a shared factor is a fabricated number), and do not write verified_on_target (S17 ban 12: this project has no target board).

rules.claim: This candidate was eliminated at G4: its pooled 99th-percentile control-step latency exceeds the deployment's control period, measured on a pinned host.
rules.condition: candidates[i].gates.G4.result == 'fail' AND measurement_environment.warning is falsy. Cite gates.G4.p99_ms against gates.G4.threshold_ms, both present in every report version. Evidence pass: rank candidates[i].episodes by p99_latency_ms and report replan_count beside the worst rows. Always carry gates.G4.caveat verbatim.
rules.suggested_action: Find where the cost is: p99_latency_ms on each candidates[i].episodes row with replan_count beside it, since every replan records a control step carrying the global planner's latency and G4 pools it with the rest. Register a candidate with a cheaper global planner, or one that replans less. Note the direction of the logic, which makes this elimination trustworthy: G4 on the host is a necessary condition, so failing here proves failing on the slower target board (HD-7.2) - it is a G4 pass, not a G4 fail, that proves nothing.
rules.forbidden_action: Do not raise robot.control_period so the budget fits the candidate - HD-7.2 documents that exact loosening and its removal, and HD-7.2's rule runs the other way: the local controller's own rate must be <= profile.robot.control_period, checked at startup. Do not apply a host-to-board conversion factor (S17 ban 8) and do not print verified_on_target or target_p99_ms (S17 ban 12, HD-7.2 sim-only reservation).

rules.claim: This candidate was eliminated at G5: its worst-episode memory estimate exceeds what the board leaves for navigation.
rules.condition: candidates[i].gates.G5.result == 'fail'. Cite gates.G5.memory_estimate_mb against gates.G5.available_ram_mb and branch the remedy on gates.G5.status. Read gates.G5.peak_search_nodes and gates.G5.bytes_per_search_node only when they resolve - to_card adds them solely for a structural resource profile, so they are absent under declared_by_author and would be dropped by keep_resolvable. Never cite gates.G5.peak_rss_mb_diagnostic as the ground for the verdict.
rules.suggested_action: Branch on gates.G5.status. Under estimated_from_structure the number is peak_search_nodes x bytes_per_search_node plus the tree, costmap and fixed-overhead terms, so bound the search: register a candidate with a smaller costmap footprint or a planner that does not expand the whole map. Under declared_by_author the figure was never measured, and HD-7.3 law 2 gives a declared figure elimination value only - which is this direction, so the elimination stands on its own terms. If available_ram_mb genuinely mis-states the board's allocation, correct hardware together with its HD-2.4 breakdown table and record why.
rules.forbidden_action: Do not raise available_ram_mb without the ram_budget breakdown that must add up to it - S17 ban 14, and HD-2.4 makes available_ram_mb an allocation decision rather than a measurement. Never substitute gates.G5.peak_rss_mb_diagnostic for memory_estimate_mb: that compares a Python process against a C++ board budget, is wrong by an order of magnitude in an unpredictable direction, and is S17 ban 13 - HD-7.3 names 'G5: pass beside peak_rss_mb: 340' as what the violation looks like. And do not treat the budget as continuous: HD-7.3 law 3 makes available_ram_mb a step function in money, so over budget means a different board class, not slightly more expensive.

rules.claim: This candidate was eliminated at G6: it requires a perception input this deployment does not declare, and no number of episodes changes that.
rules.condition: candidates[i].gates.G6 == 'fail'. There is no further evidence in the report: to_card emits G6 as a bare verdict string per HD-12, so G6Result.required, .available and .missing never reach it. The advice must say which token is missing ONLY by naming where to look, never by guessing. field_path is the verdict string itself, which resolves in every report version.
rules.suggested_action: G6 is decided before episode one, inside build_candidates - early_stop.gates_without_a_rule.G6 says so in the report - so re-running changes nothing. The stored report does not carry which token is missing, so read the candidate's observation_requirements from GET /api/v1/candidates/{candidate_id} against the deployment's available_observations. Then either register a candidate that fits the sensors the site actually has, or, if the site genuinely owns the sensor and the profile simply omitted it, add the token to available_observations. HD-7.0 guarantees this is a real incompatibility and not a spelling difference: the vocabulary is closed and an unknown token fails at parse time.
rules.forbidden_action: Do not add a token to available_observations that the site does not own. That field is a claim about the customer's hardware, and every measurement downstream then describes a robot that does not exist. Do not drop the token from the candidate's observation_requirements either: HD-1.3 hashes observation_requirements into candidate_id, so the edit produces a different candidate, and every trace, pairing and Delta-U already keyed to the old id stops describing it.

rules.claim: This run's stored report predates the per-episode table, so its gate failures can be named but not explained.
rules.condition: candidates[i].cleared_gates is False AND resolve(report, 'candidates[i].episodes') is None. Verified to affect 7 of the 11 reports under artifacts/runs, including every one written on 2026-08-11 and several on 2026-08-12. field_path is blocking_gates, which is present in every report version and is non-empty whenever cleared_gates is False.
rules.suggested_action: Re-score from the traces this run already has rather than re-simulating: run_uri names the directory and run_checksum fingerprints the files it was computed from, and the score-only path rebuilds the report from the stored Parquet without running an episode. HD-8.4 constraint 3 requires exactly this property - with no decision_utility to reproduce, re-scoring the traces must reproduce the same gate table.
rules.forbidden_action: Do not re-run the sweep to obtain the missing breakdown and then read the new gate table as an explanation of the old one. New episodes are a new sample; run_checksum exists precisely because a reference to files cannot otherwise say they are still the ones the result came from.

risks: The per-episode table is a RECENT addition and is missing from most stored runs. `candidates[i].episodes` (built by `_episode_outcomes`, selection.py:935) is absent from 7 of the 11 reports under /home/hungnguyen/projects/Project_RAV19/artifacts/runs - all four from 2026-08-11 and three of five from 2026-08-12. G1 and G3 diagnoses lean on it hardest, so every rule that reads it must degrade to a verdict-only form rather than emit nothing, and `keep_resolvable` must not be the only thing standing between the reader and silence.

The manifest is null in exactly the runs this feature is for. Verified across all 11 stored reports: every report with `decision_card == null` also has `manifest == null`. `manifest.constraints` is the only place a report carries `success_rate_min`, `no_path_rate_max`, `episode_timeout_s` and `goal_tolerance_m`. So on a gate-only run - the one where 'why did G3 fail' is the whole question - the G3 threshold is NOT recoverable from the report. The advice can state the observed value from `candidates[i].success_rate` but must not print a threshold it cannot cite.

G1, G3 and G6 carry no evidence in the stored report at all. `GateReport.to_card()` emits `self.g1.result`, `self.g3.result` and `self.g6.result` as bare strings, so `g1.no_path_rate`, `g1.threshold`, `g3.success_rate`, `g3.threshold` and `g6.required/available/missing` exist on the Python objects and never reach disk. Confirmed on a real report: `G1/G3/G6: pass fail pass`. HD-12 (CONTRACTS.md lines 874-885) pins that card shape, so widening `to_card()` is a contract change requiring a contracts_version MINOR bump in the same PR (HD-15.3). The non-breaking place to add the detail is the candidate entry in `run_comparison` (selection.py), which is not contract-pinned - but that is in packages/benchmark, outside this feature's module.

`resolve()` cannot distinguish absent from null, and `keep_resolvable` drops both. Any advice citing `gates.G2.upper_bound_95` (null once a collision is observed), `gates.G2.note` (null in the common case), `gates.G5.target_implementation` (absent under an artifact resource profile), `gate_only_deployment` (null on the normal path) or `episodes[j].failure_reason` (null on a successful episode) will vanish silently. Every field_path in this spec was chosen to be non-null under its own trigger condition; new rules must be checked the same way.

Four existing self_check rules already cover part of this ground and will double-report if the advice layer re-derives them: G2_REPLAYED_EPISODES (n_distinct < n_runs), SAMPLE_BELOW_N_MIN (run-level sample shortfall), G4_HOST_ONLY (screened_on_host disclosure) and G5_DECLARED_NOT_MEASURED. G2_TOO_FEW_DISTINCT_EPISODES and the G4 pair are the overlaps to watch; the suppression conditions are written into each rule but need a test that fires both layers on one report.

An early-stopped candidate ran fewer episodes than the survivors (`candidates[i].stopped_early`, `early_stop.stopped`, `early_stop.episodes_saved`). A failure_reason histogram computed over a retired candidate's prefix is not comparable with a survivor's, and stating a dominant bucket without the denominator repeats the mistake `candidates[i].n_episodes` was added to prevent. Any histogram must be reported with n_episodes beside it.

`_failure_reason` applies a strict precedence - collision > no_path > timeout > stuck - so an episode with both a no_path event and a collision is bucketed 'collision'. G1's numerator and the histogram therefore agree exactly (both read the same field), but both under-count no_path whenever a collision co-occurs. A diagnosis that says 'only 3 episodes failed to find a route' is precise about the field and can still understate the planner's difficulty.

Advice is rendered text, so S17 ban 10 applies to it. `assert_no_banned_language` must run over the advice payload on the way out, exactly as `GateReport.to_card` and `DecisionCard.to_json_dict` already do - the rule has to hold on every path that produces text, not the ones somebody remembered. The `do_not` strings in this spec quote contract prose that discusses safety thresholds; they are written to avoid the literal banned substrings, but the guard is what should enforce that, not the author.

`do` and `do_not` are exactly where an LLM layer would be most tempted to invent a remedy, and a fabricated remedy is more dangerous than a fabricated finding - it tells someone what to change. If an advice-with-model variant is built, it cannot reuse `critique.py`'s `_summarise`, which deliberately strips the per-episode tables this feature depends on.

The advice module must stay import-pure. packages/decision is a pure Python library (CLAUDE.md, CONTRACTS S16): the rules may read only the report dict passed in - no FastAPI, no repository, no TaskProfile lookup, no filesystem. The route text in several `do` fields is a string the rules emit, not a call they make; `advice.py`'s own docstring already states that advice never acts.
open_questions: Where do the rules live? `packages/decision/planbench_decision/advice.py` is new and untracked, exports only the shape (Advice, AdviceKind, keep_resolvable, order), and its docstring calls itself 'the shape for the second half'; `tests/test_advice.py` tests only the shape. self_check.py by contrast holds both shape and rules in one module. This spec assumes a sibling `gate_advice.py` importing the shape, which keeps the untracked file and its test untouched - confirm that rather than appending nine rule functions to advice.py.

Should `run_comparison` be extended to write G1/G3/G6 evidence into the report's candidate entry - e.g. `no_path_rate`, `success_rate_min`, `no_path_rate_max`, and G6's `missing` tokens? That is the clean fix for the three gates that carry nothing, it does not touch HD-12's card shape, and it would make G1/G3/G6 advice as well-grounded as G2/G4/G5. But it is an edit in packages/benchmark, it only helps runs made after it lands, and it needs its own approval under the phase rule.

Should the endpoint load the TaskProfile from the database to recover thresholds for card-less runs? `TaskProfileService.load(profile_id)` can do it. But the profile's constraints may have been edited since the run - the Manifest docstring is explicit that constraints may be edited in place and that the manifest is the only thing preventing two cards that disagree - so a threshold read live is not necessarily the one the verdict was computed against. If it is done at all, the profile should be merged into the source dict under a distinct key (e.g. `profile.constraints.*`) so field_paths still resolve against exactly what the reader is shown.

How should the 7 pre-episode-table reports be handled - degrade (GATE_EVIDENCE_NOT_IN_REPORT, as specified), or backfill by re-scoring their traces through the score-only path? Backfilling rewrites stored evidence and would need the run_checksum to be re-verified first; degrading leaves the oldest runs permanently thinner. This is a data decision, not a code one.

What severity does a gate failure deserve? self_check's scale is about whether a stated conclusion survives ('blocking' = the conclusion does not stand on this evidence). A gate failure is the system working correctly, not a broken conclusion, so the scale is being reused with a shifted meaning - here it reads as 'how much does this change what the reader does next'. Either confirm that reading or give Advice its own vocabulary before the two get compared in a UI.

Does this feature need an advice-with-model layer, and if so what is its MAX_MODEL_FINDINGS equivalent? `critique_with_model` is the precedent, but the model there may only add objections; here it would be adding remedies, which is a materially different authority. A defensible middle position is to let the model order and explain the deterministic advice and write the summary paragraph, while `do` and `do_not` stay rule-authored - but that is a design decision, not something the existing code settles.

tool_response: Structured output provided successfully

tool_input.feature: Pre-flight check: advisory rules that read a *draft* comparison (stored TaskProfile + the candidate specs a caller is about to POST) and report, before any episode runs, every condition that a gate would otherwise catch after tens of minutes of simulation, plus setup mistakes no gate catches at all. Never blocks, never launches, never writes. Emits frozen `planbench_decision.advice.Advice` objects with `kind="preflight"` — that model already exists, has `do`/`do_not` beside `claim`/`ground`/`field_path`, and has **no producer yet**; this feature is its first one. Citations are held to the same contract as `self_check`: every `field_path` must resolve through `resolve()` against the draft dict, or the advice is dropped (`keep_resolvable`), and the list is sorted by `order()` so two runs of one draft agree.
tool_input.module_path: packages/benchmark/planbench_benchmark/preflight.py (single home; the API route is a thin adapter). Rationale: most rules need the registry (`AlgorithmInfo.benchmarkable/requires_model/stochastic_global_planner/local_controller`), the named controller configs, and the loaded map — all of which live in `planbench_benchmark`, which already imports `planbench_decision`. Putting the rules in `planbench_decision/preflight.py` beside `self_check.py` would force `decision` to import `benchmark` and close the cycle that `gates.py` already dodges with a TYPE_CHECKING import for `planbench_metrics`. `planbench_benchmark` is a pure Python library (no FastAPI/ROS2/frontend), so the core-first rule is intact. Public surface: `PREFLIGHT_CODES: tuple[str, ...]`, `build_draft(profile, specs, *, scope, episodes, map_base_dir) -> dict[str, Any]`, `preflight(draft) -> tuple[Advice, ...]`. `preflight()` takes only the draft dict (like `critique(report)`) so it never touches disk and is trivially testable; `build_draft()` is the only part that loads a map.
tool_input.api_route: POST /decisions/preflight in apps/api/planbench_api/routers/decisions.py — request body is the existing `DecisionRequest` (task_profile_id, candidates[CandidateSpec], scope, episodes, reuse_traces) so a client can pre-flight exactly the body it is about to send to POST /decisions; 200, never 201 (nothing is created) and never 4xx on a finding (advisory). Response `PreflightResource`: {task_profile_id, scope, plan: {seed_count, episodes_per_candidate, n_min_required, episode_runs_total}, rules_applied: len(PREFLIGHT_CODES), advice: [AdviceResource{code, kind, severity, claim, ground, field_path, do, do_not}], blocking, material, disclosure}. Register it BEFORE `GET /decisions/{run_id}` is irrelevant (different method), but keep it above any future `POST /decisions/{something}` path parameter for the same reason `/task-profiles/template` sits above `/task-profiles/{profile_id}`. Counts derived from the advice list inside the resource builder, never passed in — the `_critique_resource` precedent.

This feature is the intended first producer. Severity is re-exported from self_check: blocking | material | disclosure.

The citation walker: dotted parts, `name[i]` for list indices, returns None when absent. CRITICAL TRAP: it also returns None when the value legitimately IS None, and keep_resolvable cannot tell the two apart — so no rule may cite `task_profile.constraints.cost_per_mission_max`, `task_profile.min_episodes_before_stop`, or `task_profile.replanning.max_replans` (all legitimately None). `False`, `0.0` and `[]` all survive. `critique()` is the post-hoc twin of this feature and its module docstring is the style to copy.

extra="forbid", frozen. `effective_claim_level` caps the desired claim by what the data supports: one mission => "mission"; robust_deployment additionally needs a neighborhood evaluation, which selection.run_comparison never performs (it builds only sample_set="evaluation" contexts).

Model validator already refuses seed_time_offset<=0 on waypoint/periodic/sudden_stop and offset<period on periodic, so traffic that exists is guaranteed to vary with the seed. Paths are stored as given; nothing here touches disk.

`n_min_evaluation_episodes` is a property: ceil(round(3.0/collision_probability_max, 6)). cost_per_mission_max defaults to None and only matters in decision_mode="business_adjusted", which the launch path never selects (selection.py constructs a bare DecisionSettings(), whose decision_mode defaults to "technical") — so no money rule is proposed.
control_period is the deployment REQUIREMENT (G4's threshold), distinct from a controller's own control_period. t_cycle_ms = control_period*1000.
The total-minus-breakdown arithmetic is already enforced at load (1% tolerance), so no pre-flight rule needs to restate it.
start/goal are Pose2D (x, y, theta) and accept the YAML triplet form. Probabilities must sum to 1.0 (validated); ids must be unique (validated).
`active` is a property that ORs all seven — use it, never re-derive. All default to 0/False, i.e. a quiet simulator.
Defaults to disabled. max_replans is None when unlimited — never cite it. The trigger is NOT configurable: the engine's STUCK / NO_PROGRESS verdicts are what replanning intervenes on.

data_sources.symbol: DynamicObstacle, WaypointMotion, PeriodicMotion, RandomWalkMotion, SuddenStopMotion, position_at
data_sources.notes: Every obstacle's reachable set is computable from declared geometry without simulating: periodic = the segment start->end; waypoint = the polyline (plus the closing leg when loop/ping_pong); sudden_stop = the ray from start along heading of length speed*stop_time; random_walk = the disk of radius max_radius about origin. `position_at(obstacle, time, seed)` is pure if a sampled check is preferred.
Closed two-token vocabulary, canonicalised (sorted, deduped) on both the candidate and the deployment side, so a set comparison is literal and safe.

data_sources.symbol: Candidate, StackComponent, StructuralResourceProfile, ArtifactResourceProfile, validate_experiment_scope, ExperimentScope
data_sources.notes: candidate_id hashes {type, stack (names+versions), params, observation_requirements} — NOT resource_profile and NOT tuning. ExperimentScope = global_planner_selection | local_controller_selection | full_stack_selection. validate_experiment_scope already raises on a duplicate candidate_id, on a monolithic candidate under a layer-scoped run, and on a fixed layer that differs (component, version AND params) — but it treats ANY string that is not "full_stack_selection" as layer-scoped, so a typo'd scope passes it.

Which gate reads which profile field, i.e. the map of what a pre-flight can anticipate. G2 passes only when observed_collisions==0 AND n_distinct_episodes>=n_min; n_distinct is the number of DISTINCT metric tuples (path_length_m, travel_time_s, min_clearance, near_miss_rate, collision_count, success), not the row count.

Five entries: astar+dwa, astar+ppo (requires_model=True), astar+pure_pursuit (benchmarkable=False), rrtstar+dwa (stochastic_global_planner=True), rrtstar+pure_pursuit (benchmarkable=False). Every entry today is global_observation_class=full_static_map, local_observation_class=lidar_only. `_build_ppo` refuses when find_spec("stable_baselines3") is None — an environment fact knowable before launch.

data_sources.symbol: candidate_from_stack, observation_requirements_for, _REQUIREMENTS, CONTROLLER_CONFIGS, LOCAL_CONTROLLER_CONFIGS, CONTROLLER_OF_CONFIG, DEFAULT_STRUCTURAL_PROFILE, validate_control_rate, NotBenchmarkableError, UnknownParameterError, ControlRateViolation
data_sources.notes: _REQUIREMENTS maps observation class -> G6 tokens: full_static_map=() ; lidar_only=(lidar_2d,) ; human_states=(human_state_estimates,). So every registry stack currently requires exactly ('lidar_2d',). CONTROLLER_OF_CONFIG is keyed by config name and gives the controller it belongs to — the only clean way to catch "astar+ppo with dwa_coarse", which today dies inside _reject_unknown_params with a message about parameter names. validate_control_rate INSTANTIATES the local planner to read .control_period.

evaluation_seed_count = ceil(n_min / len(missions)). build_evaluation_contexts crosses EVERY mission with EVERY seed, so total episodes per candidate = seed_count * len(missions). The API's `episodes` field is passed straight in as seed_count — it is a SEED count, not an episode count. Balanced by design; Mission.probability is deliberately ignored (the Mission Sampler is phase 2).

Already checks five things before episode one: pose outside map, pose on occupied/unknown cell, robot radius does not fit, start and goal in different connected components of the radius-eroded free space, start within goal tolerance of goal. It does NOT check clearance beyond the bare radius and does NOT look at dynamic obstacles at all. `_passable_space(map_data, radius)` is the erosion+labelling to reuse. Module-level `_CACHE` keyed on path + content digest.
width*height is exactly the costmap_cells figure the trace recorder is given, which is what makes G5's floor computable before any episode.

memory_estimate_mb (structural) = (peak_search_nodes*bytes_per_search_node + peak_tree_nodes*bytes_per_tree_node + costmap_cells*bytes_per_costmap_cell*costmap_layers)/BYTES_PER_MB + fixed_overhead_mb, with BYTES_PER_MB = 1024*1024. Setting the two node counts to 0 gives a lower bound every candidate must pay. FailureReason buckets are collision > no_path > timeout > stuck, in that precedence. _near_miss_rate counts clearances strictly < clearance_warning_m.
Confirms costmap_cells for the G5 floor, and that `stuck_time_window` is the profile's stuck_threshold_s while `progress_time_window` is NOT passed — it keeps Scenario's default.

data_sources.symbol: termination order in the step check
data_sources.notes: Order is collision -> goal -> timeout -> stuck -> no_progress, and STUCK/NO_PROGRESS need a window sample at least stuck_time_window / progress_time_window seconds old. So if stuck_threshold_s >= episode_timeout_s the STUCK verdict is unreachable, and since Scenario.progress_time_window defaults to 30.0 and the profile cannot set it, NO_PROGRESS is unreachable when episode_timeout_s <= 30.
progress_time_window is not reachable from a TaskProfile, so 30.0 is a fixed fact of every deployment — import it, do not retype the number.

Replanning fires only on STUCK/NO_PROGRESS, and _replan now plans from `get_observation()` — the docstring says the ground-truth `engine.dynamic_obstacles_now()` read was removed (HĐ-4.1). This CONTRADICTS planbench_benchmark/observation.py::global_class_under_replanning and its caller runner.py, which still upgrade the global planner's observation class on the grounds that replanning hands it ground truth. Because of that contradiction no rule about replanning changing the observation class is proposed.

Order of operations before episode one: load_task_map -> validate_missions_on_map -> build_candidates (validate_experiment_scope, validate_control_rate) -> build_evaluation_contexts. Those refusals are exceptions, not findings: the pre-flight's job for them is to state them in the draft UI instead of at launch. DEFAULT_SCOPE = "global_planner_selection". The per-candidate report block records global/local observation class per candidate and nothing compares them.

scope is a bare `str` with no Literal validation. The only pre-launch check today is `len({(stack, local_config)}) < 2`, which is a name-level dedupe, not an identity-level one. GET /decisions/{run_id}/critique is the shape to mirror for the response resource and its derived counts.

Re-filing an existing profile id with different content is refused (compared as validated TaskProfiles, not dicts). This CLOSES the otherwise-serious hole where reuse_traces=True would serve traces recorded under a different sensor_noise or replanning setting, since episode_context_id hashes only (task_profile_id, mission_id, environment_variant, seed) — so no pre-flight rule is proposed for it.

Calibration check: the rule set below fires NOTHING on open_hall_v2 and only PF_REPLANNING_OFF_WITH_TRAFFIC (disclosure) on warehouse_a_v2. That matters — self_check's own design note is that a critic which flags the system for being honest is a critic reviewers stop reading.

rules.claim: this run will produce a Decision Card under the scope that was asked for
rules.condition: plan.scope not in {"global_planner_selection", "local_controller_selection", "full_stack_selection"} (import ExperimentScope's members from planbench_decision.candidate; do not retype the strings)
rules.suggested_action: correct the scope to one of the three declared values before launching
rules.forbidden_action: do not let it run and then relabel whatever the card ends up saying — this is the sharpest late failure in the chain: DecisionRequest.scope is an unvalidated `str`, validate_experiment_scope treats any string other than "full_stack_selection" as layer-scoped (fixed_layer="global"), so a typo passes every pre-episode check, all episodes run, and DecisionCard.experiment_scope (a Literal) raises only when the card is assembled at the very end

rules.claim: this candidate set can support a conclusion about the layer the scope names
rules.condition: call validate_experiment_scope(scope, candidates) and convert ExperimentScopeViolation into advice — do not re-implement it. Fires when the scope is layer-scoped and the fixed layer's (component, version, params) fingerprint differs across candidates, or when a monolithic candidate is present
rules.suggested_action: equalise the fixed layer across candidates, or declare full_stack_selection and word the conclusion about the whole stack
rules.forbidden_action: do not widen the scope to full_stack_selection while still writing a sentence about one layer — the refusal is about what the evidence can support, not about which label parses

rules.claim: this run compares two different configurations
rules.condition: two entries of the draft share candidates[i].candidate_id. Reachable today despite the router's `len({(stack, local_config)}) < 2` check, because that dedupes NAMES: two differently-named local configs holding identical params hash to one candidate_id (candidate_id covers type, stack, params, observation_requirements — not the config's name)
rules.suggested_action: change one candidate's stack, version or parameters so the two are genuinely different configurations
rules.forbidden_action: do not rename one config to make the two look distinct in the request — the id is the identity every trace, pairing and ΔU keys on, and a candidate cannot be its own rival

rules.claim: every named stack is something this platform may recommend
rules.condition: algorithm_info(stack) is None, or info.benchmarkable is False (astar+pure_pursuit, rrtstar+pure_pursuit), or info.requires_global_path is False, or the resulting candidate is type="monolithic" (no policy registry exists, so stack_id_for refuses). Obtain this by catching UnknownAlgorithmError / NotBenchmarkableError around candidate_from_stack
rules.suggested_action: pick a benchmarkable stack from GET /algorithms (astar+dwa, astar+ppo, rrtstar+dwa)
rules.forbidden_action: do not flip benchmarkable to True for a pure-pursuit reference to fill a second slot — it ignores sensing, and recommending a controller that drives without looking is the failure the gates exist to prevent

rules.claim: the named local-controller configuration configures this stack's controller
rules.condition: CONTROLLER_OF_CONFIG[local_config] != algorithm_info(stack).local_controller (e.g. stack "astar+ppo" with local_config "dwa_coarse": every shipped config belongs to "dwa")
rules.suggested_action: choose a configuration registered for this stack's controller, or register one for it in CONTROLLER_CONFIGS
rules.forbidden_action: do not read the current failure at face value — today this dies inside _reject_unknown_params complaining about velocity_samples/omega_samples/horizon_seconds, which sends the reader to fix parameter names when the real mistake is that the configuration belongs to another controller

rules.claim: this candidate can be built and run
rules.condition: algorithm_info(stack).requires_model is True and the candidate's params block for that controller carries neither a non-empty model_id nor a non-empty model_path (PPOStackConfig._require_a_model)
rules.suggested_action: pick a model from the registry for this candidate before launching
rules.forbidden_action: do not substitute any available checkpoint to get the run started — a PPO result names exactly which weights produced it or the numbers mean nothing

rules.claim: this server can run every candidate in the set
rules.condition: any candidate has algorithm_info(stack).requires_model is True and importlib.util.find_spec("stable_baselines3") is None — the same test _build_ppo makes at build time
rules.suggested_action: install the optional RL dependencies from requirements-optional.txt on this host, or compare stacks this server can build
rules.forbidden_action: do not queue the sweep and hope — the failure lands when the first episode tries to build a planner, after the request was accepted

rules.claim: each candidate closes its control loop as fast as this deployment requires
rules.condition: call validate_control_rate(profile, candidates) and convert ControlRateViolation into advice. Fires when the built local planner's control_period > profile.robot.control_period + 1e-9 (e.g. a 0.1 s DWA against a 0.05 s deployment). GUARD: skip the build for a candidate whose stack has requires_model=True, because building it loads a checkpoint
rules.suggested_action: run the controller at the deployment's rate, or declare a deployment that only needs this one
rules.forbidden_action: do not relax robot.control_period to make it fit — that field is G4's threshold, so relaxing it widens the gate the candidate could not clear (the fossil documented at the top of warehouse_a_v2.yaml)

rules.claim: every mission is runnable on the map this deployment names
rules.condition: call load_task_map(profile, base_dir=<the same repo root DecisionRunService.run passes>, validate=True) and convert MapProfileMismatch into advice, one per problem sentence it reports: pose outside the map, pose on an occupied/unknown cell, robot radius does not fit, start and goal in different connected components, start within goal tolerance of goal
rules.suggested_action: move the offending pose onto free floor that the robot's radius fits, or derive a profile whose map supports these missions
rules.forbidden_action: do not read the resulting run as a comparison — every candidate returns no_path or succeeds at t=0, every column reads a plausible 0.00, and the report ties four stacks on a question none of them was asked

rules.claim: the map this deployment names exists where the engine will look for it
rules.condition: MapLoadError from load_environment_map — environment.map or environment.map_yaml does not resolve to a file under the base_dir the run will use
rules.suggested_action: file the map through the map store and derive the deployment (POST /task-profiles/derive), which materialises the map_server pair the engine reads
rules.forbidden_action: do not point the profile at a path that only exists on one machine — the map is part of the world the run claims to have measured

rules.claim: this candidate can be evaluated on this deployment at all
rules.condition: any token in candidates[i].observation_requirements is absent from task_profile.available_observations — G6's exact test, run before the episodes instead of after them. Today every registry stack requires ('lidar_2d',), so this fires on a deployment whose available_observations omits lidar_2d
rules.suggested_action: declare the sensor in available_observations if the site really owns that subsystem, or drop the candidate from the set
rules.forbidden_action: do not add the token to the deployment merely to clear G6 — the gate is pricing a subsystem somebody has to buy and run, not a spelling

rules.claim: this run can support the deployment's declared collision risk
rules.condition: plan.episodes_per_candidate (= seed_count * len(profile.missions)) < task_profile.constraints.n_min_evaluation_episodes. Only reachable when the caller names `episodes`; leaving it unset derives seed_count = ceil(N_min/len(missions)), which never falls short
rules.suggested_action: leave `episodes` unset so N_min drives the count, or raise collision_probability_max if the site genuinely accepts more risk
rules.forbidden_action: do not quote a rule-of-three upper bound off the smaller run — G2 will report `fail` with the bound looser than the declared risk, and that sentence is the result, not a formatting problem

rules.claim: N seeds will produce N independent observations of the collision rate
rules.condition: task_profile.environment.sensor_noise.active is False AND task_profile.environment.dynamic_obstacles is empty AND no candidate's stack has stochastic_global_planner=True AND no candidate's config sets deterministic=False. Nothing then differs between seeds, so _distinct_episode_count collapses to at most len(profile.missions) and G2's bound becomes 3/len(missions)
rules.suggested_action: declare the vehicle's real noise amplitudes, or the traffic the site actually has, before spending the machine time
rules.forbidden_action: do not raise sigma until the distinct count looks healthy — measure what a real 2D LiDAR and a real differential drive do and declare that; turning a physical constant into a knob for the statistic it feeds is the move the contract asks about

rules.claim: some candidate can reach this goal inside the episode timeout
rules.condition: for a mission, max(0.0, hypot(goal.x-start.x, goal.y-start.y) - constraints.goal_tolerance_m) / robot.max_linear_velocity >= constraints.episode_timeout_s. The straight line ignores turning, acceleration and obstacles, so it is a strict lower bound on any real traverse — when it already exceeds the timeout, no candidate can ever succeed and G3 rejects the whole field for a property of the profile
rules.suggested_action: raise episode_timeout_s above the floor, or shorten the mission
rules.forbidden_action: do not read the resulting 0% success as a statement about the planners

rules.claim: some candidate can fit this board's navigation budget
rules.condition: for a candidate with a structural resource profile: fixed_overhead_mb + (map.width * map.height * bytes_per_costmap_cell * costmap_layers) / (1024*1024) > task_profile.hardware.available_ram_mb. That is memory_estimate_mb with both node counts at zero, i.e. what the candidate pays before it expands a single search node, so G5 cannot pass for it however it behaves
rules.suggested_action: re-examine the RAM allocation on the board (the breakdown is the place to edit), or use a coarser map for this deployment
rules.forbidden_action: do not raise available_ram_mb without moving a line of ram_budget_breakdown — G5 loses its meaning if the threshold it compares against was invented

rules.claim: these candidates were shown the same world, so the difference between them is a difference between the stacks
rules.condition: the (global_observation_class, local_observation_class) pairs, or the observation_requirements tuples, are not identical across candidates. NOTHING in the decision path enforces this: selection.py records both classes per candidate and never compares them, and G6 only asks whether the deployment owns what each candidate needs — two candidates can both pass G6 while one reads human_state_estimates and the other only lidar_2d. Dormant today (all five registry entries are full_static_map + lidar_only) and precisely why it should exist before the first entry that differs
rules.suggested_action: compare candidates that read the same subsystems, or state in the conclusion that the better number belongs to the stack with more information
rules.forbidden_action: do not rank a stack reading ground-truth agent states against a sensing-only one and call the difference navigation quality

rules.claim: the number in `episodes` is the number of episodes each candidate will run
rules.condition: plan.episodes_requested is not None and len(task_profile.missions) > 1. build_evaluation_contexts crosses every mission with every seed, so episodes_per_candidate = episodes * len(missions) and total episode runs = that again times the number of candidates
rules.suggested_action: read the plan block: N seeds on M missions across C candidates is N*M*C simulated episodes, and decide against that number rather than against the one that was typed
rules.forbidden_action: do not divide the seed count by the mission count to hit a target run time — the episode budget is a consequence of the declared collision risk, and the mission set is a description of the deployment

rules.claim: G3 will test the success rate this deployment declared
rules.condition: task_profile.constraints.success_rate_min < 1.0 and success_rate_min > 1 - 1/plan.episodes_per_candidate. G3 compares successes/N >= threshold, so at that N a single failure already falls below the bar: the declared 0.98 is a 1.00 in effect
rules.suggested_action: declare 1.0 if perfection is what is meant, or run enough episodes for the declared rate to be expressible at all
rules.forbidden_action: do not read a G3 pass as evidence the declared rate was met — at this sample size it is evidence that nothing failed

rules.claim: G1 will test the no-path rate this deployment declared
rules.condition: 0 < task_profile.constraints.no_path_rate_max < 1/plan.episodes_per_candidate. G1 compares no_path/N <= threshold, so the effective bar is zero no-path episodes
rules.suggested_action: state that the run allows no no-path episode at all at this sample size, or run more episodes
rules.forbidden_action: do not raise no_path_rate_max after seeing which candidate tripped it

rules.claim: replanning is switched on for this run, so a blocked stack can recover
rules.condition: task_profile.replanning.enabled is True AND constraints.episode_timeout_s <= constraints.stuck_threshold_s AND constraints.episode_timeout_s <= Scenario's progress_time_window default (30.0, import it — a profile cannot set it). The engine checks timeout before stuck and before no-progress, and both need a window sample that old, so neither of the two replan triggers can ever fire
rules.suggested_action: lower stuck_threshold_s below episode_timeout_s (and keep the timeout above 30 s) so the triggers can fire, or turn replanning off and say so
rules.forbidden_action: do not report the run as having measured stacks under replanning — the config was declared and inert, and the manifest will record it as on

rules.claim: the failure_reason column distinguishes a stuck robot from a slow one
rules.condition: task_profile.constraints.stuck_threshold_s >= task_profile.constraints.episode_timeout_s. Timeout is evaluated before the stuck check in the engine step, so a wedged robot is always reported as `timeout` and never as `stuck`
rules.suggested_action: set stuck_threshold_s well below episode_timeout_s so a wedged episode ends when it wedges
rules.forbidden_action: do not read the absence of `stuck` rows as evidence that nothing got stuck

rules.claim: this run measures how these stacks handle the traffic the deployment declares
rules.condition: task_profile.environment.dynamic_obstacles is non-empty and task_profile.replanning.enabled is False (the default, and the state every stored run was measured under)
rules.suggested_action: state that what is compared is one-shot global paths under traffic, with recovery left entirely to the local controller — or enable replanning, which applies to every candidate alike
rules.forbidden_action: do not enable replanning for one candidate and not another; it is a property of the evaluation conditions, not a capability a stack owns

rules.claim: arriving at this goal is a normal arrival for a robot of this size
rules.condition: the goal (or start) cell is passable at radius but not at radius + constraints.clearance_warning_m — reuse task_map._passable_space with the enlarged radius, or a distance transform of the free mask. validate_missions_on_map only checks the bare radius, so a goal that fits by a centimetre passes it while every candidate ends its episode inside the near-miss threshold
rules.suggested_action: move the goal into a pocket with clearance_warning_m of room, or state that near_miss_rate for this deployment includes the arrival itself
rules.forbidden_action: do not compare near_miss_rate across candidates as a property of their controllers when the geometry guarantees it for all of them

rules.claim: no candidate is placed where the declared traffic will be
rules.condition: a mission start or goal lies within robot.radius + obstacle.radius of an obstacle's reachable set, computed from declared geometry only — periodic: the segment start->end; waypoint: the polyline plus its closing leg when loop/ping_pong; sudden_stop: the ray from start along heading of length speed*stop_time; random_walk: the disk of radius max_radius about origin. validate_missions_on_map never looks at dynamic obstacles
rules.suggested_action: move the pose or the obstacle's path so the robot is not parked in a traffic lane
rules.forbidden_action: do not read the resulting collisions as a ranking signal — every candidate is hit at the same place for the same reason, and G2 eliminates the whole field for a property of the profile

rules.claim: the declared traffic is what makes one seed differ from another
rules.condition: no obstacle's reachable set (same geometry as PF_POSE_INSIDE_TRAFFIC) comes within robot.radius + obstacle.radius + constraints.clearance_warning_m of the straight segment from start to goal, for any mission. HEURISTIC: the driven path is not the straight line, so word it as a check, never as a fact
rules.suggested_action: stage one episode on the test bench and watch whether the robot and the obstacle ever share a corridor; if they do not, the seeds vary in nothing that reaches the metrics and G2's n_distinct will collapse
rules.forbidden_action: do not treat the presence of a dynamic_obstacles block as proof the evaluation set has independent draws — the reference warehouse shifted a 24 s patrol by 6 s, no seed ever met the forklift, and 100 episodes collapsed to one while looking entirely normal

rules.claim: the reported numbers describe this deployment's workload
rules.condition: len(task_profile.missions) > 1 and the probabilities are not all equal (max - min > 1e-6). build_evaluation_contexts is balanced by design and deliberately does not weight by Mission.probability — the Mission Sampler is a later phase
rules.suggested_action: read every aggregate as an unweighted average over missions, or re-weight the declared probabilities by hand when quoting a deployment-level figure
rules.forbidden_action: do not quote a deployment-level average from a balanced sample as though it followed the declared mission mix

rules.claim: the card from this run may print the claim level the profile asks for
rules.condition: task_profile.claim_level != profile.effective_claim_level(neighborhood_evaluated=False). Two ways in: one mission with claim_level "deployment"/"robust_deployment", and any "robust_deployment" at all — selection.run_comparison builds only sample_set="evaluation" contexts and never runs a neighborhood evaluation, so the robust level is unreachable through this path
rules.suggested_action: add the missions the level needs, or declare the level the run can support
rules.forbidden_action: do not read the recommendation as deployment-wide because the profile asked for it — the level printed is computed from the data provided, never taken from the input

rules.claim: near misses will be counted for this deployment
rules.condition: task_profile.constraints.clearance_warning_m == 0.0 (the field allows ge=0). _near_miss_rate counts clearances strictly below the threshold, and clearance <= EPS is already a collision, so at zero the metric can never fire
rules.suggested_action: declare the clearance the site treats as a near miss
rules.forbidden_action: do not read near_miss_rate = 0 for every candidate as evidence that nothing came close

rules.claim: this deployment owns the subsystems it declares
rules.condition: a token in task_profile.available_observations is required by no candidate in the set
rules.suggested_action: state that the run does not exercise that subsystem, so nothing here justifies the cost of owning it
rules.forbidden_action: do not present a passing G6 as evidence the declared sensor was needed

risks: The draft dict is the contract. Every field_path in the rules above resolves against exactly one shape — {"task_profile": profile.model_dump(mode="json"), "candidates": [...], "plan": {...}, "map": {...}} — and `keep_resolvable` silently deletes any advice that misses it. Freeze that shape in `build_draft()` and test each rule's citation against it, the way tests/test_advice.py already tests the mechanism.

resolve() cannot distinguish 'field absent' from 'field is None', so keep_resolvable drops advice citing a legitimately-null field. `constraints.cost_per_mission_max`, `min_episodes_before_stop` and `replanning.max_replans` (None means unlimited) are all null in normal profiles. None of the rules above cites one; a later rule easily could, and it would vanish without a trace.

Three rules (PF_SCOPE_CANNOT_HOLD_LAYER_FIXED, PF_CONTROL_RATE_SLOWER_THAN_DEPLOYMENT, PF_MISSION_MAP_MISMATCH) must be produced by CALLING the existing validators and converting their exceptions, not by re-implementing their logic. A second copy of validate_experiment_scope's fingerprint comparison or of validate_missions_on_map's erosion is exactly the two-definitions drift the architecture puts one owner on each schema to prevent.

validate_control_rate instantiates the local planner to read its control_period. For a stack with requires_model=True that means loading a checkpoint inside what is supposed to be a cheap advisory call. Guard the build, or read the declared control_period out of the candidate's params block for that controller and say in the ground sentence which of the two was used.

The map-dependent rules (PF_MISSION_MAP_MISMATCH, PF_MAP_UNREADABLE, PF_G5_FLOOR_ABOVE_BUDGET, PF_GOAL_CLEARANCE_TIGHT) need the same base_dir DecisionRunService.run passes to run_comparison (the repo root). Resolve it from the same dependency, or the pre-flight will report a missing map that the run then finds, which destroys trust in every other finding.

PF_TRAFFIC_NEVER_MEETS_MISSION and PF_GOAL_CLEARANCE_TIGHT are geometric heuristics over a straight line and an eroded mask, not over the path a planner will drive. They can be wrong in both directions. Keep them at material, word the ground as an observation and the `do` as a check (the test bench stages one episode without measuring anything), and never phrase them as 'will'.

Calibration is the whole risk of an advisory layer. Verified against the shipped deployments: nothing fires on open_hall_v2, and only PF_REPLANNING_OFF_WITH_TRAFFIC (disclosure) fires on warehouse_a_v2. Any new rule should be checked the same way — self_check deliberately stays silent when the card already says NEAR_EQUIVALENT, because a critic that flags the system for being honest stops being read.

PF_ZERO_VARIANCE_SEEDS reasons about determinism of the whole stack. It is sound for today's registry (A* deterministic, RRT* seeded per episode via stochastic_global_planner, PPO with deterministic=True). A future controller that draws randomness without declaring it would make the rule claim zero variance where there is some — the safe direction is a false alarm, but the inference should be written against the declared flags (stochastic_global_planner, PPOStackConfig.deterministic) rather than against a hardcoded list of planner names.

PF_MODEL_NOT_CHOSEN, PF_RL_RUNTIME_MISSING and PF_CONFIG_NOT_FOR_THIS_CONTROLLER are correct but currently dormant in practice: LOCAL_CONTROLLER_CONFIGS holds only dwa_* entries, so astar+ppo cannot be registered through the API at all today and PF_CONFIG_NOT_FOR_THIS_CONTROLLER fires first. Write them, expect them not to fire, and do not 'simplify' them away later on the evidence that they never fired.

Advisory means advisory. If POST /decisions ever starts refusing on a blocking pre-flight finding, this stops being an advisory reader and becomes an unreviewed gate — and several of its rules are heuristics that must never have that power. Keep the launch endpoints untouched.
PREFLIGHT_CODES must be published beside the results (the RULE_CODES precedent), so an empty list reads as 'the rules ran and found nothing' rather than 'no rules ran'.
open_questions: Home of the module. I recommend packages/benchmark/planbench_benchmark/preflight.py because the registry, the controller configs and the map loader all live there and benchmark already imports decision. The alternative — profile-only rules in planbench_decision/preflight.py beside self_check.py, registry/map rules in benchmark — is closer to the stated precedent but splits one feature across two homes, which is the shape the codebase argues against elsewhere ('two producers of one artifact'). Confirm before writing.

Does the pre-flight need to accept an unsaved profile body? POST /decisions takes a stored task_profile_id, so the route above can only check a filed deployment. The obvious use — warn while somebody is still typing the deployment form — would need a second body shape accepting the profile document inline. Not proposed here.

Contradiction found while verifying, unresolved, and it blocks one rule I would otherwise propose: planbench_benchmark/observation.py::global_class_under_replanning (used by runner.py) upgrades the global planner's observation class when replanning is on, on the stated grounds that replanning hands it ground-truth obstacle positions — while services/simulator/planbench_simulator/nav_stack.py::_replan says that ground-truth read was removed and it now replans from get_observation() per HĐ-4.1. If nav_stack is current, the upgrade table and its caller are stale; if the upgrade is current, a candidate under replanning is using information G6 never priced (candidate_from_stack derives observation_requirements from the static registry declaration). Someone should settle which is true before any rule speaks about replanning and observation classes.

Should the pre-flight advice be recorded on the report when a run does go ahead (so GET /decisions/{id}/critique can see what was known before launch), or stay purely a separate call? Storing it would let a reviewer see that a blocking pre-flight finding was raised and the run was launched anyway — which is exactly the kind of thing HĐ-14 keeps a journal for — but it also makes the report carry an advisory that a later rule change would leave stale.

Is a model layer wanted on top, mirroring critique_with_model? Advice carries the same citation contract, so the same resolve()-checked, fabricated-counted arrangement would work unchanged. Out of scope as written.

PF_SUCCESS_RATE_GRANULARITY has a policy edge: open_hall_v2 documents that its honest success_rate_min is 1.00 and that it says 0.95 only because a 1.00 threshold collapses the anchor scale (KNOWN_LIMITATIONS L6). At N=30 the rule stays quiet there (1 - 1/30 = 0.967 > 0.95), but if that threshold is ever revisited the rule and the anchor argument will meet. Worth knowing before the rule surprises someone.
